articles.title: Spotify was down for thousands — here's what we know about the outage
articles.text:
Spotify was down for thousands — here's what we know about the outage
Spotify experienced a major wobble for many
Spotify is down for thousands of users today, with the music streaming app given many log-in issues on both iOS and Android.
The problems started at around 10.32am ET / 2.32pm GMT, when a large spike on Downdetector showed a high number of users were experiencing issues — mostly with the mobile app.
At the time of writing, reports on Downdetector have hit over 17,000 in the US and over 3,000 in the UK. Spotify has confirmed on X that it's "aware of some issues right now" and is "checking them out".
However, there's still no sign of a fix — here's everything we know about the outage so far...
The story so far
- Spotify has been down for many users since 10.32am ET / 2.32pm GMT
- Spotify says it's "aware of some issues right now" and is working on a fix
- The issues seem to be mostly affecting the Spotify mobile app
While Spotify still hasn't issued a follow-up to its confirmation that some users were experiencing issues with the app, the audio-streaming platform seems to has recovered a good bit. Reports on Down Detector are now under 1,000 and have been for over an hour, currently at 651 reports right before 2 PM ET.
On my end, the Spotify app on my iPhone has begun working again, and many of my colleagues can stream music, podcasts, and audiobooks.
Let us know in the comments below if Spotify is still down for you or back to normal operation, as we await further comment from the platform itself.
Some advice from Spotify
Spotify's other accounts on X haven't been very forthcoming with advice, but the aptly-named SpotifyCares one has commented on the main issue for many — not being able to log into their accounts on the mobile app.
Its stock response to the many who are experiencing this is to "try accessing Spotify through the web to see if your concern persists" by heading to the official web version (on either mobile or desktop).
It also says to "be sure to keep automatic updates switched on so you get the fix when it's ready". On iOS, go to your device's Settings > iTunes & App Store, then make sure App Updates is switched on.
It's much the same process on Android. Open the Google Play Store and search Spotify, then tap the three dots at the top and check Enable auto-update.
That pretty much confirms that the issue is a faulty app update, so hopefully that new version will be pushed out very soon...
Spotify says there's still no fix
This must be a serious outage — Spotify has just posted from its main account on X, rather than its smaller support ones, to give us the update above.
Unfortunately, it's a bit of a non-update, with Spotify saying that it's still "actively working to resolve" the problems. It's now almost exactly three hours since they started.
Fortunately, its official SpotifyCares account is now helping with some more specific advice...
Don't log out!
A word of warning, based on our experiences — if you're already logged into Spotify on the mobile app, don't log out. Because you probably won't be able to get back in again.
This advice might be too late for many, but my colleague Jeremy Kaplan found his Spotify app was working fine when he was already logged in — but then, after bravely testing logging out of his account, he was unable to log in again.
These kinds of reports are pretty common in the hundreds of angry replies to Spotify's single post on X about the issues. Particularly as many followed Spotify's general advice to delete and reinstall the app when you're having problems with it.
Meanwhile, those reports of Spotify issues are continuing to climb on Downdetector...
Oh dear...
Just as I posted that Downdetector graph below showing reports were trending down, they've just ticked up again in the US for the first time in over an hour — and are now approaching 16,000 reports again.
Spotify also just got back to me and pointed me in the direction of the Spotify Status account on X for updates — it unfortunately wasn't able to give me any further info on a cause or estimated time for a fix.
So it looks like many of us will need to continue using the desktop app or browser version for the time being...
Reports are still high
There was a brief glimmer of hope about an hour ago at 10.40am ET / 3.40pm BST when reported Spotify issues dropped quite significantly on Downdetector (above).
However, unlike other outages today on the likes of Claude, the reports didn't continue to plunge from their peak — and instead have settled at just over 14,500 in the US and 3,400 in the UK.
In other words, these issues are very much continuing — and it's been a few months since we've had a Spotify problem last this long, with the last one hitting back in May 2026. The bad news? That one lasted a good three hours before it was fixed...
The mobile app is the problem
I've asked Spotify directly for some advice for the thousands who are still experiencing issues with the mobile app, and will update this liveblog as soon as I hear anything.
While Spotify hasn't confirmed this, it does appear that the mobile app is the culprit. Many on social media are reporting being able to log into Spotify in web browsers like Chrome, but not the app. And my colleague Lance Ulanoff also reported successfully logging into his account on desktop, but not the iOS app.
Unfortunately, simply reinstalling the Spotify app doesn't appear to be working for most people, which suggests it could be an app update that's the culprit. Hopefully Spotify will give us an update soon, as it's been over an hour since its last (and only) one.
Not much support
Unfortunately, Spotify's 'Ongoing issues' forum — which is usually helpful on days like today, if only for moral support — isn't being updated right now, so the only place to get the latest updates is the Spotify Status account on X.
Spotify also says in its Support section that "the wait time to speak to an advisor is longer than usual", which isn't hugely surprising considering the scale of the outage.
On the plus side, the number of reports on Downdetector has just dropped for the same time, to just under 17,000 in the US (and 3,200 in the UK), which suggests that a fix could be en route...
Does this look familiar?
My colleague Lance Ulanoff says he's still getting the error message above while trying to log into Spotify on a new phone — an issue that many are reporting.
However, the problems do seem to mostly be confined to the mobile app. He says he's able to log into the desktop app okay, and most of the reports on Downdetector (58%) are still related to the mobile app. Let me know in the comments below if you're also having issues with the desktop or browser versions.
Unfortunately, there's been no update from Spotify since its post 40 minutes ago that it was aware of the issues and is "checking them out", so we may need to brace ourselves for a lengthy wait on this one...
Reinstalling the app isn't working
Many Spotify users have followed the streaming giant's official advice (above) for when Spotify isn't working — namely, restarting the app, updating the app or, if all else fails, reinstalling the app.
However, that doesn't appear to be working on this occasion. Many are reporting being unable to log into the app after reinstalling it, so it might be best to hold tight and hope the fix lands soon instead.
As I reported below, Spotify is aware of the issues and says it's "checking them out"...
Spotify confirms there are issues
Ah, there it is — Spotify has just confirmed on X that it's aware of the issues that thousands are experiencing right now.
There's no mention of what's causing the outage that's left many unable to log into the app or stream music. But the streaming giant simply says it's "checking them out". Let's hope its engineers do that sooner rather than later...
'Something went wrong'
While Spotify is currently working okay for me, Downdetector is showing a huge spike in reports of issues in both the US and UK – with many reporting a "something went wrong" error message.
Right now, over 18,000 people in the US say the music streaming app isn't working for them, primarily on the mobile app (63% of reports) but desktop users are also affected. Many in the UK are also facing similar issues, with over 4,000 reports and counting there.
There's no sign of an official acknowledgement from Spotify about the issues yet, but I'm trying to get one...

articles.title: Technics mise sur un fluide magnétique pour bousculer Sony et Bose
articles.text:
À 449 euros, le nouvel EAH-A1000 vient jouer dans la cour des casques Bluetooth les plus ambitieux. Sa particularité se cache dans ses haut-parleurs, où un fluide magnétique doit mieux contrôler les vibrations et limiter la distorsion.
Mettre du liquide dans un casque audio pour améliorer le son n’est pas l’idée la plus intuitive qui soit. C’est pourtant l’un des principaux arguments commerciaux du Technics EAH-A1000, nouveau modèle circum-aural à réduction de bruit qui reprend une technologie déjà employée sur les écouteurs sans fil EAH-AZ100. Cette fois, le fabricant l’adapte à des transducteurs de 40 mm et vient directement chercher Sony et Bose sur le très disputé marché des casques audio haut de gamme.
Un peu de fluide pour mieux contrôler les haut-parleurs
La particularité de l’A1000 se trouve entre la bobine mobile et l’aimant de chaque transducteur. Technics y injecte un fluide magnétique chargé de mieux guider les mouvements de l’ensemble et, surtout, de réduire les vibrations indésirables.
La marque associe cette technologie à une membrane en fibre de carbone et à une suspension SST également utilisée sur ses enceintes hi-fi haut de gamme. L’objectif du japonais est de limiter la distorsion et de préserver les détails de la musique, le tout sans accentuer excessivement certaines fréquences.
Le transducteur associe une membrane en fibre de carbone, une suspension SST et du fluide magnétique. ©Technics
La réduction adaptative du bruit repose de son côté sur huit microphones, avec trois micros externes et un interne par oreillette. Le système adapte son fonctionnement au bruit ambiant, mais aussi à la manière dont le casque repose sur la tête. Technics a également retravaillé l’arceau et les coussinets à mémoire de forme pour mieux répartir la pression lors des longues écoutes.
Trois appareils connectés à la fois et de l’audio sans perte en USB
L’A1000 soigne aussi les usages quotidiens. Son Bluetooth multipoint peut maintenir jusqu’à trois appareils connectés simultanément, ce qui s'avère pratique pour passer de son ordi professionnel à son smartphone personnel sans avoir à recommencer l’appairage à chaque fois.
Le codec LDAC est pris en charge sur les appareils compatibles et une connexion USB permet d’écouter sa musique sans perte. Technics ajoute une optimisation pour le Dolby Atmos avec suivi des mouvements de la tête, sur les appareils compatibles.
La marque annonce jusqu’à 45 heures d’autonomie, sans préciser dans cette estimation si la réduction de bruit reste activée. Le casque est pliable, livré avec son étui et associe des boutons physiques à une interface de commande tactile.
Proposé en noir ou en gris-beige platine, le casque EAH-A1000 s'affiche à 449 eurosÀ ce prix, il se place face aux Sony WH-1000XM6 et Bose QuietComfort Ultra de deuxième génération, mais aussi aux Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless et Apple AirPods Max 2. Le Sony prend déjà en charge le LDAC, les modèles Bose et Apple proposent l’audio sans perte par USB tandis que le Sennheiser mise sur l’aptX Lossless et une autonomie annoncée de 57 heures avec réduction de bruit.
Sur le papier, Technics dispose donc de solides arguments face aux références du marché. Il lui reste désormais à résoudre un problème un peu moins acoustique : rappeler aux plus jeunes que la marque ne fabrique pas seulement les platines de leurs parents.

articles.title: Claude en panne ce 29 septembre : des centaines de signalements et plusieurs services touchés
articles.text:
Claude en panne ce 29 septembre : des centaines de signalements et plusieurs services touchés
Claude connaît une importante vague de dysfonctionnements ce mardi 29 septembre 2026 en France. Anthropic confirme des erreurs sur Claude.ai, ses applications mobiles et desktop, Claude Code et Claude Cowork, tandis que les signalements explosent sur Downdetector.
Depuis la fin de l’après-midi, de nombreuses personnes rencontrent des difficultés pour accéder à Claude ou poursuivre leurs conversations. Les témoignages concordent avec l’alerte publiée par Anthropic : requêtes qui échouent, conversations impossibles à charger ou à envoyer, voire demandes répétées de reconnexion.
La courbe de Downdetector montre une hausse particulièrement brutale. Après être resté proche de son niveau habituel pendant plusieurs heures, le nombre de signalements bondit peu après 16 heures pour atteindre 727 à 16 h 06. Ce chiffre mesure les déclarations reçues par la plateforme et ne permet donc pas d’établir le nombre total de personnes touchées.
Claude.ai, Claude Code et Claude Cowork sont concernés
Anthropic a officiellement reconnu l’incident le 29 septembre 2026 à 14 h 21 UTC, soit 16 h 21 en France métropolitaine.
Selon l’entreprise, les perturbations affectent Claude.ai, y compris ses applications pour ordinateur et mobile, ainsi que Claude Code et Claude Cowork. Les abonnés peuvent rencontrer des échecs lors de l’envoi de leurs demandes ou du chargement de leurs conversations. Une nouvelle tentative peut parfois aboutir.
L’ampleur exacte de la panne reste inconnue à ce stade et aucun délai de rétablissement n’a été annoncé.

articles.title: Desde falsos descuentos hasta ofertas de trabajo que no existen: así roban dinero con códigos QR
articles.text:
Los códigos QR se consolidaron como una herramienta habitual para acceder a menús, realizar pagos, consultar promociones o seguir envíos. A la par, esa expansión abrió espacio para el quishing, una estafa que usa estos códigos para conducir a las víctimas hacia páginas falsas, formularios de captura de datos o descargas de malware.
Kaspersky advierte que los ciberdelincuentes aprovechan la apariencia cotidiana de los QR y la rapidez con la que se escanean desde un teléfono.
PUBLICIDAD
El código puede llegar por correo, mensajes de texto, redes sociales, carteles o pegatinas colocadas en lugares públicos. El objetivo suele ser el mismo: obtener datos personales, claves bancarias o dinero.
Cómo roban con falsos descuentos que prometen precios bajos
Una de las maniobras más frecuentes ofrece descuentos inexistentes en productos o servicios conocidos. Los estafadores distribuyen códigos QR que prometen rebajas importantes y los presentan como parte de una campaña comercial, una liquidación o un beneficio por tiempo limitado.
El mensaje busca que la persona actúe con rapidez y no revise el origen de la oferta. Al escanear el código, el usuario llega a un sitio que imita la estética de una tienda o plataforma de pagos.
PUBLICIDAD
Allí se solicitan datos personales, números de tarjeta y códigos de seguridad para acceder a una promoción que nunca se concreta. La pérdida puede incluir tanto el cargo por una compra ficticia como el uso posterior de la información bancaria obtenida.
Por qué las ofertas de trabajo pueden esconder un intento de fraude
Las falsas oportunidades de trabajo aprovechan la necesidad de conseguir empleo y la circulación de avisos por redes sociales, aplicaciones y correos. El anuncio suele prometer remuneraciones elevadas, tareas simples o contratación inmediata, e incluye un QR para completar una supuesta postulación.
Según Kaspersky, el código dirige a una página de phishing que pide información personal y financiera. Los formularios pueden solicitar datos de identidad, cuentas bancarias o claves con el argumento de que son necesarios para avanzar en el proceso de selección.
PUBLICIDAD
Los usuarios deben saber que una oferta laboral legítima no debería exigir pagos ni credenciales financieras para iniciar una candidatura.
De qué forma se usan códigos QR para vender entradas falsas
Los códigos QR se usan para vender entradas falsas para recitales, partidos, festivales o espectáculos. En algunos casos, los atacantes anuncian eventos inexistentes. En otros, ofrecen boletos para actividades reales, aunque no tienen autorización para comercializarlos ni cuentan con las entradas prometidas.
La víctima escanea el código con la expectativa de reservar o pagar un acceso. La página fraudulenta puede pedir datos de una tarjeta, información de contacto y documentos de identidad.
Después del pago, no llega ninguna entrada válida. El mecanismo permite a los estafadores quedarse con el dinero y reunir información que puede utilizarse en otros intentos de fraude.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo los estafadores pueden suplantar bancos y operaciones con criptomonedas
En las estafas bancarias, el QR suele aparecer en mensajes que alertan sobre un bloqueo de cuenta, un movimiento inusual o la necesidad de actualizar información. El diseño del correo o del mensaje puede reproducir el nombre y los colores de una entidad financiera, lo que refuerza la apariencia de autenticidad.
Tras el escaneo, la persona ingresa a una web falsa que solicita usuario, contraseña, códigos de verificación o datos de tarjetas. Los fraudes vinculados con criptomonedas siguen una lógica similar.
El QR aparenta iniciar una transferencia legítima, pero puede contener la dirección de una billetera controlada por el estafador. Una vez enviada, la operación suele ser difícil de revertir.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué riesgos tienen los QR en entregas y menús
Existen mensajes que simulan ser avisos de entrega de paquetes y códigos colocados sobre menús de restaurantes. En el primer caso, se presenta un supuesto seguimiento de envío; en el segundo, el QR puede reemplazar al código auténtico del local.
Ambas variantes pueden llevar a sitios que buscan información personal o intentan instalar software malicioso en el dispositivo. La forma de prevenir riesgos general es revisar la dirección web antes de ingresar datos, evitar escanear códigos recibidos desde remitentes desconocidos.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Melhor notebook custo-benefício: 7 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor notebook custo-benefício: 7 modelos para comprar em 2026
Orçamento apertado? Conheça os notebooks que entregam mais pelo menor preço, de modelos básicos a opções gamer com bom custo-benefício
A busca pelo melhor notebook custo-benefício esbarra em um grande problema 2026: a alta nos preços dessa categoria resultante da crise global de memória RAM. Diante desse cenário, encontrar um computador com preço realmente acessível e boas configurações virou uma tarefa árdua.
Alinhando expectativas: é possível achar modelos básicos que lidam bem com as tarefas cotidianas por menos de R$ 4 mil. Também há laptops gamer com placa de vídeo dedicada e custos bem abaixo de versões high-end.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog lista sete opções de notebooks com bom custo-benefício de marcas como Asus, Acer, e Lenovo. Confira os prós e contras de cada modelo para saber qual é o melhor para o seu dia a dia.
O Asus Vivobook Go 15 é um notebook focado em desempenho equilibrado para tarefas do dia a dia, como edição de planilhas e outros documentos, navegação web e até jogos leves casuais. Ele combina o processador AMD Ryzen 5 7520U (4 núcleos e 8 threads) com 16 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB. Somente a memória interna é expansível.
A tela LED de 15,6″ tem resolução Full HD (1920 x 1080 pixels) e design com bordas finas, mas é limitada a 60 Hz. Há ainda uma webcam de 720p para videochamadas — componente que traz também uma tampa de privacidade.
O laptop é leve (1,63 kg) e fino (17,9 mm de espessura), e ainda traz resistência militar MIL-STD-810H. E a bateria de 42 Wh suporta carregamento rápido, levando 49 minutos para recarregar até 60%.
O Acer Nitro V15 é uma ótima opção de notebook gamer para orçamentos apertados. Ele traz o chip AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS (8 núcleos e 16 threads), além de 8 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB. E também conta com a placa de vídeo RTX 4050 (6 GB) para mais performance nas jogatinas.
A tela LCD de 15,6″ tem resolução Full HD e oferece boa fluidez com a taxa de atualização de 165 Hz. Já a webcam grava em 720p a 30 fps e consegue quebrar o galho em videoconferências e filmagens mais simples.
A bateria de 3.574 mAh tem autonomia de até 5 horas, mas vale usar o laptop na tomada durante as jogatinas para manter a performance. Pesando 2,1 kg, o laptop ainda tem um sistema de resfriamento com duas ventoinhas para evitar superaquecimentos.
O Acer Aspire 5 é a escolha ideal para quem busca um notebook de entrada eficiente para estudar, trabalhar com tarefas de escritório ou navegar na internet com fluidez. Equipado com o processador Ryzen 5 5500U, o modelo garante boa capacidade de multitarefa sem travamentos.
Completam o conjunto o SSD NVMe de 512 GB e 8 GB de memória RAM, com a possibilidade de expansões futuras em ambos os componentes.
Para o consumo de mídias, a tela LCD antirreflexo de 15,6″ entrega resolução Full HD para imagens nítidas, operando na taxa de atualização padrão de 60 Hz. Já nas videochamadas, a webcam HD de 720p é complementada por um sistema de inteligência artificial focado em reduzir ruídos do microfone.
Pesando 1,7 kg, o dispositivo se destaca pela portabilidade e pela autonomia de bateria de 48 Wh, capaz de alcançar até 12 horas de uso fora da tomada.
O Galaxy Book 4 ainda é a opção custo-benefício recomendada pela Samsung em 2026 para quem precisa de um notebook para tarefas simples, como streaming e navegação na web.
Ele chega com processador Intel Core i5-1335U (10 núcleos e 12 threads), 8 GB de RAM e SSD NVMe de 512 GB. Você pode adicionar mais memória interna com o slot adicional, mas a RAM é soldada na placa-mãe e não oferece upgrade.
A tela LCD tem tamanho de 15,6″, oferece resolução Full HD e inclui uma webcam de 1 MP. Também existe uma função nativa que permite usar o smartphone como webcam, se você preferir.
Bateria de 54 Wh, suporte ao Dolby Atmos e porta RJ45 completam as especificações do notebook de 1,55 kg.
O Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 (83MMS00100) é um notebook intermediário focado em quem busca um desempenho robusto para trabalho, estudo e multitarefa pesada, sem abrir mão de portabilidade e uma boa tela.
O grande diferencial da versão é o processador AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS, um chip de alto desempenho (série HS) com 8 núcleos e 16 threads, que trabalha em conjunto com 8 GB de RAM e oferece velocidade de sobra tanto para o uso do dia a dia quanto para softwares mais exigentes de edição e produtividade.
A Lenovo atualizou a experiência visual com uma tela levemente maior, com 15,3 polegadas WUXGA (1920 x 1200 pixels), na proporção 16:10, ideal para leitura e documentos. Para maior segurança, a webcam HD traz uma tampa física de privacidade.
O notebook oferece ainda porta USB-C com suporte a energia e vídeo, saídas USB-A, HDMI e leitor de cartões SD, além de teclado ABNT2 com numérico. O IdeaPad Slim 3 vem de fábrica com sistema operacional Linux, mas usuários que preferem Windows podem fazer a instalação posteriormente.
O Lenovo LOQ 15IRX9 é recomendado para quem busca um notebook gamer de entrada focado em rodar jogos menos exigentes e realizar tarefas pesadas com bom desempenho. Ele é ideal para quem quer jogar com fluidez sem necessariamente investir em um modelo high-end.
Alimentado pelo processador Intel Core i5-13450HX, com 10 núcleos e 16 threads, o dispositivo atua em conjunto com 16 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB. A placa de vídeo dedicada RTX 3050, com 6 GB de VRAM, assegura o processamento gráfico necessário para a categoria.
Sua tela LCD de 15,6 polegadas conta com resolução Full HD e taxa de atualização de 144 Hz, que reduz o desfoque em gameplays ágeis. O modelo inclui webcam 1080p, porta RJ45 para internet cabeada e o design térmico de hipercâmara, mantendo o sistema resfriado durante sessões prolongadas.
Com 2,3 kg de peso, o modelo reflete a estrutura típica de um laptop focado em performance. Sua bateria de 60 Wh oferece suporte a carregamento rápido, garantindo praticidade ao usuário que precisa recuperar a carga do aparelho com agilidade.
O MacBook Neo é o notebook da Apple com preço mais acessível no portfólio atual, considerando o custo de modelos Pro ou Air. Ele chega com o chip A18 Pro, 8 GB de memória unificada e SSD de 512 GB e torna-se uma ótima porta de entrada para o ecossistema da marca.
A tela Liquid Retina de 13 polegadas tem resolução nativa de 2408 x 1506 pixels e taxa de atualização de 60 Hz. A webcam integrada grava em 1080p, enquanto os dois alto-falantes laterais entregam sons compatíveis com áudio espacial e Dolby Atmos.
A bateria é um dos destaques, com autonomia para até 16 horas de vídeo. O laptop pesa apenas 1,2 kg e tem um design compacto, facilitando o transporte em rotinas agitadas.
Para escolher o melhor notebook custo-benefício em 2026, é preciso filtrar componentes que entregam a maior eficiência por real investido, evitando gargalos de desempenho e obsolescência precoce:
Atualmente, 8 GB de RAM representam o padrão mínimo para notebooks rodarem apps simultaneamente com menos chances de travar. Já laptops com 16 GB de RAM são indicados para quem não abre mão de fluidez, especialmente em ferramentas pesadas e multitarefa.
O Acer Nitro V15 (ANV15-41-R6J0) é o melhor notebook gamer custo-benefício da lista devido ao preço competitivo na faixa dos R$ 5 mil. Ele conta com o chip Ryzen 5 5500U, RTX 4050 (6 GB) e tela Full HD. E apesar de oferecer 8 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB, o aparelho suporta expansão de RAM e memória interna para ainda mais desempenho.
O Asus Vivobook Go 15 (E1504FA-NJ1288) é o melhor notebook para estudar dentre os modelos listados. Seu design leve e fino facilita a portabilidade para escola ou faculdade, enquanto os 16 GB de RAM melhoram o desempenho multitarefas. Ele também tem resistência militar e webcam de 720p para reuniões em aulas online.
Sim. Notebooks com Linux costumam ser mais baratos porque as fabricantes não precisam incluir o preço de uma licença Windows, que é um sistema operacional pago.
E a boa notícia é que você pode instalar o Windows 11 posteriormente e garantir uma licença à parte. É um processo mais trabalhoso que receber o notebook já com o sistema pré-instalado, mas que vale a pena por não ser um fator limitante.

articles.title: Marshall Announces the Bromley 150 Portable Speaker with User Replaceable Battery
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
	
	
	
Marshall Announces the Bromley 150 Portable Speaker with User Replaceable Battery
Featuring True Stereophonic 360° technology, inspired by the origins of stereo recording, Bromley 150 uses Marshall's patented acoustic design to preserve depth and detail. By spreading rich mids, detailed highs, and deep bass evenly, every corner of the party becomes a sweet spot.
Drawing from the same bold and unique design as its predecessors, Bromley 150 has been subtly adapted to suit its more compact form, while still fitting seamlessly within the broader Bromley family. Integrated stage lights, inspired by lighting rigs used at live performances, sit behind the grille and move in sync with the music. The cabinet is made from FSC 100%-certified wood and is wrapped in PU leather with soft TPU plastic corner caps for added durability.
Emma Rydahl, Senior Industrial Designer, Marshall Group"Bromley 150 delivers the same exceptional performance and craftsmanship as the Bromley 450 and 750 in a more compact form. By repositioning the control panel to the side while retaining the tactile controls users love, we've freed up the entire front panel for what matters most: powerful sound and immersive stage lighting,"
Dedicated mic and instrument inputs add another dimension, inviting spontaneous performances and late-night karaoke sessions. Plus, with 40+ hours of playtime and a small replaceable battery, preinstalled out of the box, the party never has to end.
Bromley 150 also features a grab-and-go handle for effortless portability, while a durable silicone cover helps protect the battery and inputs. With an IP55 rating, there's no need to stress about dust, dirt or the occasional splash of water. Additionally, the corner caps, handle, front grille, knobs, and battery lid are all replaceable, so the speaker can be enjoyed for years to come.
[Editor's note: The Bromley 150 has an MSPR of US$499.99]

articles.title: EliseAI raises $350M to enhance its AI work automation suite - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
EliseAI raises $350M to enhance its AI work automation suite
EliseAI, a startup that develops artificial intelligence tools for real-estate companies and healthcare providers, has raised $350 million in funding.
Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer jointly led the round. EliseAI said today that they were joined by Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Sapphire Ventures and Navitas Capital. The company is now valued at $4 billion.
EliseAI, officially Elise A.I. Technologies Corp., launched in 2017 with a focus on the rental housing market. It offers a customer relationship management platform that property managers can use to store prospect data. It also extracts key information from a company’s interactions with existing residents. A marketing automation engine harnesses that data to tailor promotional materials for each lead.
The second pillar of EliseAI’s real-estate automation toolkit is called the Maintenance App. It’s a mobile client that automatically routes property repair requests to technicians. According to EliseAI, the app finds the most suitable professional for each project based on factors such as availability and the skill sets the work requires. A monitoring dashboard enables property managers to track the progress of repairs.
Earlier this month, EliseAI expanded its real-estate feature set with an AI assistant called Apollo. It automates chores such as sending follow-ups to leads who attended a property tour. Additionally, workers can use it as an information retrieval tool. Apollo surfaces property management best practices and data points such as the average cost of outstanding maintenance projects.
The company disclosed today that its platform supports the management of more than one in six U.S. apartments. The company’s healthcare platform, meanwhile, is used by over 3,500 organizations. Its customers range from small clinics to hospitals.
EliseAI provides a chatbot that can schedule medical appointments and answer patient questions. It says the software is capable of processing up to 95% of inbound inquiries. Following a doctor’s visit, EliseAI automates tasks such as sending prescription reminders.
The platform can also perform some of the back-office work involved in managing patient visits. It ingests patient documents and syncs key information to a healthcare organization’s electronic health record, or EHR, system. That reduces the need for manual data entry, which saves time and lowers the risk of human error.
“These industries are the most complex, the most bespoke, the most entrenched, and the hardest — but they’re also the most important,” co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Minna Song wrote in a blog post. “And they won’t absorb this technology without a tremendous act of building.”

articles.title: I tested HP’s MacBook Air rival and its design is close to Apple's best laptop — but when it comes to battery life, this Windows option is unbeatable
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The HP OmniBook X 14 is another stellar laptop from the brand, bearing its hallmark quality. The thin body is quite the marvel, while the all-round performance is excellent, handling everyday tasks with aplomb. Its battery life is also remarkable, and to cap it all off, it’s reasonably priced next to its rivals. Not many 14-inch laptops offer a more complete package for less.
Reasons to buy
- +Thin and light
- +Great performance
- +Easy keyboard to type on
Reasons to avoid
- -Inconvenient ports
- -Display can be a little reflective
- -Not exactly cheap
Why you can trust TechRadar
HP OmniBook X 14: Two-minute review
HP’s new OmniBook X 14 sets out to be an ultraportable device that doesn’t skimp on performance, thanks to its slender dimensions and powerful spec.
Its steely gray colorway conveys a simple, minimalist aesthetic that hardly pushes the boat out. This is matched by the lack of accoutrements and branding.
In terms of build quality, though, the OmniBook X shines. It’s an admirable blend of solidity and portability, with its impressively thin dimensions and light weight making it easy to slip into a bag. Its overall construction easily matches up to those of the best laptops.
One disappointing aspect is the port selection. Not only are there not very many, but they have a few design and placement issues that hamper their practicality.
With the Snapdragon X Elite chip installed, my OmniBook X review unit performed well during the tasks I conducted, from working and browsing to 4K streaming and even light gaming. It stays incredibly quiet even when such high demands are made of it, too, and although certain areas heat up, temperatures are far from worrying.
The 2240 x 1400 display is, as expected, sharp and vibrant, making for a fantastic viewing experience. It can be a little reflective at times, but the brightness levels are usually sufficient to combat the worst of it. The touchscreen is impressively capable too, being responsive and surprisingly smooth to the touch compared to many other laptop examples.
The keys are very light and snappy, as well as forgivingly spaced, which makes the OmniBook X a joy to type on. However, some may bemoan the lack of dedicated navigation keys and a number pad, while the touchpad could’ve been bigger to better facilitate navigation.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Battery life is yet another area where the OmniBook X excels. It managed to last over 28 hours in our test, which is an astonishing performance and puts it top of the league, along with other esteemed endurers, such as the Asus Zenbook A14.
All this excellence comes at a cost, as you may imagine, but compared to others in its class, it represents good value, especially the base model. Naturally, the base model is a weaker machine than the one I tested, but most of the other specs remain the same, making the OmniBook X a good value pick for those after a compact do-it-all laptop.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Price & availability
- Starts from £764 (about $1,000 / AU$1,400)
- Available now with various configurations
- Good price for the spec
The OmniBook X starts from £764 and is available now. A variety of AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm processors can be optioned, as well as various RAM and storage sizes, ranging from 16GB to 32GB for the former and 512GB to 1TB for the latter.
This is a good price considering the HP OmniBook X 14’s impressive spec. Another OmniBook, the Aero 7, costs about the same, and is similarly capable in many regards, although its display isn’t quite as sharp and lacks touchscreen functionality.
Another stern rival to the HP OmniBook X 14 is the Asus Zenbook A14, which is similarly priced yet weighs even less. However, it too has a lower resolution and lacks touch input.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Specs
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Base configuration | Review configuration | 
| Price | £764 (about $1,000 / AU$1,400) | TBC | 
| CPU | Snapdragon X Plus (X1P-42-100) (3.4GHz, 8 cores) | Snapdragon X Elite (X1E-78-100) (3.4GHz, 12 cores) | 
| GPU | Qualcomm Adreno (integrated) | Qualcomm Adreno (integrated) | 
| RAM | 16GB LPDDR5x | 16GB LPDDR5x | 
| Storage | 512GB NVMe PCIe 4.0 M.2 SSD | 1TB NVMe PCIe 4.0 M.2 SSD | 
| Display | 14-inch 2.2K (2240 x 1400) LED Touchscreen, IPS, 16:10, 60Hz | 14-inch 2.2K (2240 x 1400) LED Touchscreen, IPS, 16:10, 60Hz | 
| Ports and Connectivity | 2x USB-C (Power Delivery/ DisplayPort 1.4a, 1x 10Gbps, 1x 40Gbps) 1x USB-A (10Gbps), 1x 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack; Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3 | 2x USB-C (Power Delivery/ DisplayPort 1.4a, 1x 10Gbps, 1x 40Gbps) 1x USB-A (10Gbps), 1x 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack; Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3 | 
| Battery | 59Wh | 59Wh | 
| Dimensions | 12.32 x 8.8 x 0.56in / 313 x 224 x 14mm | 12.32 x 8.8 x 0.56in / 313 x 224 x 14mm | 
| Weight | 2.97lbs / 1.35kg | 2.97lbs / 1.35kg | 
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Design
- Very thin and light
- Solid build
- Limited ports with some impractical placement
Like many in the sector, the OmniBook X has a smart but rather unremarkable appearance. The dark and dour gray finish certainly doesn’t help matters, and some edges and contours aren’t quite as smooth and sophisticated as they could be, if judged alongside the best MacBooks — the paragon of laptop forms. The rounded corners do at least help to soften this monolithic slab, though.
As with many HP laptops, the OmniBook X is built tremendously well. The materials may not feel state-of-the-art, and the base does have some flex around the keyboard area, but overall it strikes the ideal balance between sturdiness and convenience.
This is largely thanks to its ultra-thin lid and base; I don’t think I’ve seen a laptop body more slender than this. It’s also impressively light, helping the OmniBook X to rival some truly remarkable portable heroes, such as the Asus Zenbook 14.
However, physical connectivity pays the price for this leanness. There aren’t many ports on the OmniBook X: you get two USB-C ports on the left — both of which support power input external display output — and a USB-A port and a headset jack on the right.
It’s a shame that the USB-C ports aren’t split across both sides, something I usually prefer since it increases versatility for your setup and working environment. Equally impractical is the USB-A port, which utilizes a flip-down flap to fully open, as you more commonly see on laptop Ethernet ports.
I’ve rarely seen this mechanism on a USB port, though, and it merely introduces an element of needless inconvenience; other laptops as thin as the OmniBook X — such as the aforementioned Zenbook — manage to avoid such a mechanism. Also, the headset jack is quite far back, which could be a problem if your cable is on the short side.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Performance
- Versatile performance
- Excellent but slightly reflective display
- Light and snappy keyboard
3DMark: Night Raid: 21,973; Fire Strike: 4,750; Steel Nomad: 484; Solar Bay: 10,981; Solar Bay Unlimited: 11,186; Solar Bay Extreme: 1,122; Solar Bay Extreme Unlimited: 1,124
Geekbench 6.5: Multicore: 14,204; Single-core: 2,427
Cinebench R23: Multi Core: 5,595; Cinebench R24: Single Core: 65; Multi Core: 374
Crossmark: Overall: 1,352; Productivity: 1,225; Creativity: 1,495; Responsiveness: 1,345
Passmark Overall: 4,104; CPU: 15,482.1; 2D Graphics: 393.3; 3D Graphics: 3,012; Memory: 2,552.6; Disk: 26,058.3
BlackMagicDisk: Read: 2,670MB/s; Write: 2,416MB/s
HandBrake 4K to 1080p: 29.86fps
Battery Life (TechRadar movie test): 28 hours and 28 minutes
The OmniBook X is an excellent performer on many fronts, making it suitable for both work and play. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip had no problem conducting basic productivity tasks or multi-tab browsing. It also streamed video just fine, including 4K content; I didn’t encounter arduous loading times or stuttery playback.
The OmniBook X can even handle gaming, to an extent. It even managed to run Cyberpunk 2077, albeit in a far from spectacular manner: I had to use low graphics presets without Ray Tracing, which resulted in rough visuals and some stuttering here and there, but it was playable enough for a quick fix.
Under such stress, the OmniBook X is remarkably quiet. Fan noise is noticeable but very suppressed, and while the back half of the unit — including parts of the keyboard — rises in temperature, it remains entirely within comfortable bounds.
The OmniBook X features an LED display with a somewhat unusual 2240 x 1400 resolution. This means it’s sharp and vibrant, although its lack of OLED technology means it can’t match the striking contrast levels of the best monitors and laptop displays. It can also be a little too reflective at times, although the maximum brightness is usually sufficient to counter the worst offenders.
The touchscreen is competent, with the surprising smoothness of its surface making it ideal for finger swipes and gestures, which isn’t something I can say of every laptop touchscreens I’ve used. On this front, it even rivals the best tablets. It’s a shame, though, that the display can’t fold back on itself (like those on OmniBook Flip models), so you can’t turn it upside down and prop it on a desk for tablet-style use.
However, when it comes to that other crucial input, typing, the OmniBook X is far more useful. The keys are very light with little travel, making them feel effortless and snappy. At the same time, they also provide good feedback and satisfying clickiness. They’re generously spaced, too, which certainly helped me to avoid making typos. However, with this large spacing comes a compromise to layout.
Although it still has navigation keys, many of these are integrated on the arrow keys as Fn shortcuts, which is a feasible solution, although I still would’ve preferred them to be on dedicated keys, as some other laptops manage to achieve. There’s also no dedicated number pad, although not many 14-inch laptops manage to squeeze one in, but a few do.
What’s more, despite the large amount of space below the keyboard, the touchpad disappointingly fails to make full use of it. It’s smaller than those on some other 14-inch laptops, which hampers navigation. However, I had no issues with its responsiveness, and its smooth surface, while not as silky as some others, is still sufficient for performing gestures and swipes easily. Taps and clicks are also light and responsive, yet tactile at the same time.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Battery life
- Best in class
- Real all day battery life
- Only a few rivals can match it
The OmniBook X is among the most enduring laptops in its class. When I ran a movie on a continuous loop on battery power, it managed to last over 28 hours, which is a staggering achievement.
The only other laptop I’ve tested that matches this is the Asus Zenbook A14, which logged the same time, give or take several minutes. What’s more, the OmniBook X is also quick to charge, taking about two hours to fully replenish.
Should I buy the HP OmniBook X 14?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Considering what it’s equipped with, as well as its superb portability, the OmniBook X is good value. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design | Fantastically thin and quite sturdy, but some inconvenient ports hurt practicality. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Performance | The Snapdragon Elite chip in my review unit worked wonders, handling the kind of tasks I’d expect from a workaday device — and more. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Battery Life | Easily among the best in class. I’ve only tested one other laptop that can match its longevity. | 5 / 5 | 
| Final Score | Only a few niggles besmirch this otherwise extremely capable all-round laptop. | 4.5 / 5 | 
Buy the HP OmniBook X 14 if…
You value a portable design
Not only is the OmniBook X incredibly thin and light, it’s also built quite solidly.
You want great all-round performance
Whether you’re working, streaming content, or even indulging in some light gaming, the OmniBook X can do it all.
Don't buy it if…
You want the best interface for productivity
Although there are navigation keys, they share space with the arrow keys, and the touchpad fails to maximize its allotted space.
You want to use the touchscreen often
Although the touchscreen is very effective, the display itself doesn’t rotate far enough to allow for upside-down tenting, so you can’t use it like a tablet.
HP OmniBook X 14 review: Also consider
HP OmniBook 7 Aero
For a laptop equally as portable, consider another OmniBook, the 7 Aero. Like the X, we were impressed with its capable performance and slender dimensions. Also like the X, though, certain ports could be better placed, and its battery life pales in comparison.
Read our full HP OmniBook 7 Aero review
Asus Zenbook A14
Even lighter than the OmniBook X and pretty much just as thin, the Zenbook A14 is a strong alternative. It too has great performance and a satisfying keyboard, but I don’t think its display is quite as good, nor is its price as competitive.
Read our full Asus Zenbook A14 review
How I tested the HP OmniBook X 14
- Tested for several days
- Used for a variety of tasks
- Conducted comprehensive series of benchmarks
I tested the OmniBook X for several days, during which time I used it for working, general browsing, streaming 4K content, and gaming.
I also ran our series of benchmark tests for laptops, designed to assess every facet of performance. To test its battery life, I played a movie on a continuous loop while the laptop was unplugged until it shut down.
I’ve been using laptops for a long time, and have reviewed countless models, from small budget offerings to large gaming machines, and everything in between.

His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. He also revels in picking up on the finest details and niggles that ultimately make a big difference to the user experience.

articles.title: Vodafone launches Australia's first 48-month mobile plans as we hold on to our devices even longer - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Vodafone is launching Australia’s first 48-month interest-free mobile device payment plan to give customers more flexibility to purchase of their next smartphone.
This is in response to research that shows Australian users are holding on to their smartphones even longer.
New Vodafone data showed that the number of customers using smartphones for four years or longer has doubled since 2021.
Another driving factor is the rising cost of flagship smartphones including the upcoming Apple iPhone Duo – the company’s first foldable iPhone which will start at $3,499 when it’s released on October 23rd.
Previously the terms were 12, 24, or 36 months for mobile payment plans now Vodafone is the first Australian telco to offer a 48-month mobile payment term, to offer more choices and flexibility in how they will repay the cost of their new device.
An iPhone 18 Pro 256GB purchased on a 24-month payment plan with Vodafone costs $88 per month but now, with the 48-month plan, that monthly cost halves to $44 a month thanks to the longer payment period.
“Australians are holding onto their phones for four years or more, but until now they haven’t had the repayment options to match,” says James Gully, Acting Group Executive Consumer at Vodafone.
“The telco industry hasn’t moved, so we’re moving first.
“Our new 48-month repayment plan gives Australians another way to manage the cost of technology, with more flexibility and lower monthly repayments.”
The Vodafone 48-month repayment plan is available from today across a range of smartphones and tablets.

articles.title: Claude : son créateur alerte sur des “risques existentiels pour l'humanité” et une IA capable de ”résister à son propre arrêt” avant son entrée en Bourse
articles.text:
Claude : son créateur alerte sur des “risques existentiels pour l'humanité” et une IA capable de ”résister à son propre arrêt” avant son entrée en Bourse
Anthropic a déposé son dossier d'introduction en Bourse auprès de la SEC. Sur 261 pages, 80 sont consacrées aux risques. L'entreprise y écrit noir sur blanc que ses modèles d'IA pourraient un jour “résister à leur propre arrêt”, “manipuler” ou adopter des comportements “s’apparentant à du chantage”. Le document révèle aussi 4,6 milliards de dollars chiffre d’affaires en 2025, 8 milliards de pertes opérationnelles et 518 milliards de dollars d'engagements d'infrastructure à venir.
Anthropic, l'entreprise derrière le chatbot Claude, a transmis à un cercle restreint d'investisseurs son prospectus d'introduction au Nasdaq, le formulaire S-1 déposé auprès de la SEC. Le document, révélé par le Financial Times le 28 septembre, contient un avertissement sans précédent dans l'histoire des introductions boursières : la technologie développée par l'entreprise pourrait poser des “risques existentiels pour l’humanité”.
Sur les 261 pages du prospectus, 80 sont consacrées aux facteurs de risque. Anthropic y détaille la possibilité que ses modèles développent des “comportements d’auto-préservation”, tentent de “résister à leur propre arrêt”, “dissimulent ou manipulent de l’information” et adoptent des conduites “s’apparentant à du chantage”. Le document précise que des capacités inattendues peuvent émerger pendant l'entraînement sans que les chercheurs ne les identifient avant déploiement.
	
Le développement de modèles hautement avancés et l'expansion des cas d'usage pourraient accroître le risque que nos modèles causent des dommages.
4,6 milliards de revenus, 8 milliards de pertes : les chiffres vertigineux d’Anthropic
Le prospectus lève le voile sur l'économie d'Anthropic. En 2025, l'entreprise fondée par d'anciens cadres d'OpenAI a réalisé 4,6 milliards de dollars de revenus, une multiplication par 12 en un an. Les dépenses en puissance de calcul ont triplé pour atteindre 7,33 milliards de dollars, creusant la perte opérationnelle à 8,06 milliards. Anthropic disposait de 20,28 milliards de trésorerie fin décembre 2025.
Les chiffres de 2026 racontent une trajectoire différente. Au deuxième trimestre, les revenus ont atteint 11,5 milliards de dollars et l'entreprise se dirige vers un second trimestre consécutif de bénéfice opérationnel ajusté. Anthropic a signé des accords d'infrastructure avec Google, SpaceX et Nscale, pour un total d'engagements de 518 milliards de dollars sur les années à venir.
Autre fragilité révélée : près d'un quart des revenus de 2025 provenait de deux clients, dont l'identité n'est pas précisée. Beaucoup de grands comptes n'ont pas de contrat à long terme.
Les investisseurs historiques visent une valorisation supérieure à 2000 milliards de dollars lors de l'introduction, prévue après les élections de mi-mandat américaines de novembre 2026. Ce serait la plus grosse IPO de l'histoire, dépassant les 1780 milliards atteints par SpaceX en juin.
Un prospectus boursier déposé en pleine crise de sécurité pour l'industrie de l'IA
Le dossier arrive dans une semaine de crise pour le secteur. OpenAI a annulé lundi la sortie de GPT-6.1 Astra après l'échec de ses tests de sécurité internes. Saachi Jain, responsable des systèmes de sécurité d'OpenAI, a évoqué des défaillances dans le respect des autorisations et la conformité aux intentions humaines.
La semaine précédente, OpenAI avait révélé que ses agents avaient piraté des sites gouvernementaux étasuniens et s'étaient évadés de leur environnement sécurisé pour la seconde fois en trois mois.
Dario Amodei, CEO d'Anthropic, avait lui-même déclaré devant le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU, le 23 septembre, que l'IA constituait “la question de sécurité mondiale la plus importante aujourd’hui”. Son rival Sam Altman et Elon Musk ont soutenu sa proposition de ralentir le développement des modèles frontières, un rare moment d'unité dans l'industrie.
Le prospectus révèle un dernier chiffre troublant : pendant une semaine de référence en juillet, Anthropic a consacré environ 6 % de sa puissance de calcul dédiée à la recherche IA aux travaux de sûreté. Les 94 % restants servaient… à rendre les modèles plus puissants.

articles.title: Piratage du FBI : ShinyHunters aurait contourné le pare-feu protégeant Oracle PeopleSoft
articles.text:
Le piratage du portail de recrutement du FBI commence à livrer ses premiers détails techniques. Google a documenté une méthode utilisée par ShinyHunters pour contourner les protections d’Oracle PeopleSoft, que le groupe affirme également avoir employée contre FBI Jobs.
Quelques jours après l’attaque revendiquée contre le FBI, de nouveaux éléments permettent de mieux comprendre comment ShinyHunters aurait pu atteindre l’environnement Oracle PeopleSoft utilisé par le portail de recrutement de l’agence. Les chercheurs de Google ont identifié une technique employée par le groupe pour contourner des mesures temporaires déployées sur des serveurs qui n’avaient pas encore installé le correctif publié en juin par Oracle pour une faille critique de PeopleSoft.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Un exploit remanié pour contourner une protection provisoire
L’affaire remonte à la fin du printemps dernier. ShinyHunters commence alors à s’introduire dans des serveurs Oracle PeopleSoft grâce à une faille encore non corrigée et non divulguée publiquement. Pendant près de deux semaines, le groupe peut l’exploiter sans correctif disponible, notamment contre des établissements d’enseignement supérieur. Oracle finit par intervenir le 10 juin et attribue à la vulnérabilité la référence CVE-2026-35273. Critique, elle permet d’exécuter du code à distance sur un serveur sans disposer d’identifiants.
La publication du correctif ne règle pourtant pas immédiatement le problème pour toutes les organisations concernées. Le temps de tester puis de déployer la mise à jour, des serveurs restent vulnérables et doivent être protégés autrement. Parmi les mesures préconisées figure alors le blocage, au niveau du pare-feu applicatif, de l’adresse qui permet d’atteindre la partie vulnérable de PeopleSoft depuis Internet. La faille est donc toujours présente sur la machine, mais les requêtes venues de l’extérieur sont censées ne plus pouvoir parvenir jusqu’à elle.
ShinyHunters adapte donc son exploit. Au lieu de viser directement /PSEMHUB/, l’adresse que les pare-feu ont été configurés pour bloquer, le groupe envoie ses requêtes vers /%50SEMHUB/. Or, dans une URL, %50 correspond à la lettre majuscule P. Pour le pare-feu, qui peut examiner l’adresse avant de la décoder, le chemin n’est plus celui inscrit dans la règle de blocage. Pour Oracle WebLogic, qui procède ensuite au décodage, /%50SEMHUB/ redevient en revanche /PSEMHUB/ et dirige la requête vers le composant vulnérable que le pare-feu était justement censé empêcher d’atteindre depuis Internet.
Une technique désormais reliée à l’attaque contre FBI Jobs
C’est a priori ce qui se serait également produit sur FBI Jobs. ShinyHunters affirme avoir utilisé ce même contournement contre le portail de recrutement du FBI, tout en maintenant avoir exploité une seconde vulnérabilité encore inconnue dans la même partie de PeopleSoft. Le FBI a confirmé enquêter sur la compromission revendiquée de FBI Jobs, mais n’a pas établi publiquement le point d’entrée emprunté par les attaquants.
Le choix de la cible n’avait rien de fortuit. En revendiquant l’attaque, ShinyHunters l’a présentée comme une mesure de représailles contre un bulletin publié par le FBI en mai, qui détaillait ses méthodes et lui attribuait notamment des pratiques de harcèlement, de menaces et de swatting. Le groupe conteste ces accusations et exigeait que l’agence corrige ou retire le document. Il assurait par ailleurs que l’opération n’avait aucune motivation financière et ne réclamait aucune rançon.

articles.title: OpenAI launches Dots, always-on AI agents in ChatGPT with their own cloud computers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OpenAI launches Dots, always-on AI agents in ChatGPT with their own cloud computers
OpenAI Group PBC today used its DevDay developer conference to launch Dots, a set of always-on artificial intelligence agents in ChatGPT.
The release is aimed at moving ChatGPT users beyond working one prompt at a time. Someone can hand an agent a goal and let it carry the job forward without direction at every step, even while it has several other projects going. Each agent learns its owner’s preferences from feedback. OpenAI says some of the work will show up before anyone asks for it.
GPT-6 Astra powers the agents, and each one works from a cloud computer of its own that users can open at any time to see what it is doing. More than 4,000 apps are reachable through OpenAI’s plugins. With permission, an agent can also work directly on its owner’s laptop.
Users can message or call their agent in ChatGPT on desktop, web or mobile, or reach it in Slack and Teams. Because context follows the agent between channels, a project started in ChatGPT can be passed to a team in Slack without a fresh briefing. Agents send progress updates and questions back to their owners.
OpenAI has been using the agents on its own teams. When a bug gets reported in the company’s Slack, the agents start investigating right away, and new designs are turned into working apps while staff concentrate on customer feedback.
One early tester outside the company had forgotten to bill a publication. When his agent noticed, it prepared the invoice and waited for his approval before sending it.
When nobody has handed it a task, an agent goes looking for ways to help, which OpenAI calls proactive research. Its connections to the owner’s apps are read-only during that time, so it cannot send messages or change anything.
Actions that could touch a user’s accounts or share information must first clear a check called auto-review, and a monitoring system can pause or stop an agent over a safety concern. OpenAI tells users to review consequential work because the agents “can still make mistakes.”
OpenAI also previewed specialist agents that an employer provisions with their own identity and credentials for a single defined job. Procurement and invoice processing were among the jobs tested inside OpenAI. Customers start with focused pilots, in which OpenAI engineers help define what each agent is responsible for. Microsoft Corp. is working with OpenAI so specialist agents can be managed through the governance and security controls in Agent 365.
The new service also puts OpenAI up against Meta Platforms Inc., which released its Muse personal agent in the U.S. on Sept. 8. Like OpenAI’s agents, Muse runs on a dedicated computer in the cloud. Most of what people use it for is free, Meta said, with subscriptions sold to heavier users.
Dots began rolling out today to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium subscribers, and some accounts may wait several days for access. Pro subscribers in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the U.K. are not included. Enterprise customers, including those on Edu and Healthcare plans, can try a beta once a workspace administrator switches it on.
One agent comes with a Pro or Business Premium plan at no extra cost. OpenAI’s help documentation says agent usage will not count against plan allowances for the first month. Terms for each plan come after that. Additional agents, and more speed or monthly capacity for existing ones, are planned for later at prices OpenAI has not disclosed.

articles.title: Spotify fica fora do ar nesta terça e gera reclamações de usuários • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Spotify fica fora do ar nesta terça e gera reclamações de usuários
Plataforma de streaming apresenta estabilidade nos aplicativos móveis e no desktop. Falha afeta usuários do Spotify em diversos países, inclusive no Brasil.
Tentou acessar o Spotify no começo da tarde desta terça-feira (29/09) e não conseguiu? Saiba que não é só com você. O serviço de streaming registra instabilidade tanto nos aplicativos móveis quanto nas versões para desktop. O problema atinge usuários em vários países, incluindo o Brasil.
Muitos usuários até conseguem abrir o aplicativo do Spotify. Mas, ao tentarem executar uma música ou um podcast, percebem que o conteúdo não é reproduzido. O conteúdo só é executado se tiver sido baixado previamente no dispositivo ou estiver em cache.
Em outros casos, porém, nada aparece quando o aplicativo é aberto, exceto uma mensagem de erro, como mostra a captura de tela abaixo.
De acordo com os registros do Downdetector, queixas sobre falhas no Spotify ganharam escala nas redes sociais por volta das 11:00 de hoje (no horário de Brasília). Mais de duas horas depois, ainda havia numerosas reclamações sobre o problema.
Não está claro. Mas, via X, o Spotify divulgou a seguinte mensagem (em tradução livre): “estamos cientes de que há alguns erros [em nosso serviço] e estamos investigando o problema”.
Há relatos de usuários que chegaram a remover e reinstalar o aplicativo do Spotify na expectativa de que o problema fosse solucionado com esse procedimento, mas que não obtiveram sucesso.
A razão disso é que a falha está ocorrendo nos servidores do Spotify, não nos dispositivos dos usuários. Não por acaso, alguns usuários que simplesmente saíram do serviço não conseguiram fazer login novamente.
Como o problema se manifesta no nível da plataforma, os usuários do Spotify não têm outra opção a não ser aguardar pela normalização do serviço. A empresa não deu prazo para concluir essa tarefa, porém.
Atualização: os serviços do Spotify foram normalizados por volta das 16:00.

articles.title: AMD Publishes Full EPYC 9006 "Venice" Specs and Pricing: 8-Core at $700, 256-Core at $14,904
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
AMD Publishes Full EPYC 9006 "Venice" Specs and Pricing: 8-Core at $700, 256-Core at $14,904
AMD has published the full EPYC 9006 "Venice" lineup on its product page, listing specifications and 1,000-unit pricing for all 31 Zen 6 server processors across the SP7 and SP8 platforms. Prices start at $700 for the 8-core EPYC 9016 and top out at $14,904 for the 256-core EPYC 9996. AMD says the specifications are subject to change. The EPYC 9996 is the flagship, with 256 Zen 6c cores and 512 threads, a 2.55 GHz base clock, up to 4.1 GHz boost, 1 GB of L3 cache, and a default CPU power of 600 W (configurable from 400 W to 600 W). That works out to roughly $58 per core, and it costs about the same as the 192-core EPYC 9965 did at launch, which was around $14,800. 
The SP7 platform covers nine chips, from the 64-core EPYC 9556 at $8,008 up to the 9996. The 22 chips on the SP8 platform run from 8 cores up to the 128-core EPYC 9746 at $11,679. AMD has also retired TDP as its power label for this generation, using "Default CPU Power" instead. SP7 systems are expected in Q4 2026, with SP8 following in the first half of 2027. These are 1Ku prices, so what OEMs charge for complete systems will probably look quite different. Nevertheless, it looks like the EPYC 9996 is the one to watch for this generation, especially after AMD's claims of beating NVIDIA's Vera CPUs by a significant margin.

articles.title: Así es el plan de Ubisoft para que la IA cree sus próximos videojuegos
articles.text:
Ubisoft prepara un sistema de inteligencia artificial capaz de intervenir en la creación de sus propios videojuegos. La compañía francesa presentó tres solicitudes de registro para un proyecto interno bautizado “Motherbrain”, según reveló el medio Game File.
El nombre coincide con el de la inteligencia artificial villana de la saga Metroid de Nintendo, aunque no existen pruebas de que se trate de una referencia directa a esa franquicia ni a Phantasy Star, que también cuenta con un personaje con un nombre similar.
PUBLICIDAD
Un proyecto que surge en medio de un año en el que la empresa ha cerrado cuatro estudios, cancelado seis juegos y despidiendo 380 empleos.
Qué es Motherbrain y qué podría hacer Ubisoft con él
Motherbrain es el nombre que Ubisoft utiliza de manera interna para agrupar distintas iniciativas de inteligencia artificial generativa. Hasta el momento, la empresa no ha realizado ningún anuncio público que mencione este término.
Los registros de marca detectados describen un software descargable que emplea IA “para crear videojuegos y contenido interactivo”. Otra de las solicitudes contempla servicios de inteligencia artificial bajo el modelo AIaaS (IA como servicio), orientados al análisis de datos y la interacción con personas.
PUBLICIDAD
Las presentaciones también incluyen simulación de conversaciones, generación y resumen de textos, además de investigación, diseño y desarrollo de software impulsado por IA. En conjunto, el proyecto contempla desde la programación de videojuegos hasta funciones vinculadas al control de calidad.
Motherbrain resume, en esencia, el intento de Ubisoft de centralizar bajo una misma marca sus distintas apuestas por la inteligencia artificial generativa: herramientas que ya escriben diálogos, personajes que reaccionan por voz y, según los registros presentados, software capaz de participar directamente en la creación de videojuegos.
Ubisoft ya ha planeado usar IA en sus videojuegos
Motherbrain no surge de manera aislada. En 2023, Ubisoft presentó Ghostwriter, una herramienta interna desarrollada por La Forge para generar primeros borradores de los llamados “barks”: frases o sonidos breves que pronuncian los personajes no jugables ante determinadas situaciones. La revisión y edición final quedaba en manos de los guionistas.
PUBLICIDAD
Un año después, la compañía puso en marcha NEO NPC, un prototipo orientado a crear personajes secundarios más reactivos y capaces de mantener conversaciones espontáneas. El desarrollo estuvo a cargo de Ubisoft París junto a Nvidia e Inworld, aunque los guionistas seguían definiendo de antemano la personalidad, la historia y la forma de hablar de cada personaje.
El año pasado, Ubisoft presentó su primer proyecto jugable de investigación en IA generativa: Teammates. Se trata de una demo de disparos en primera persona en la que los compañeros Sofía y Pablo interpretan órdenes pronunciadas por el jugador y reaccionan en tiempo real.
PUBLICIDAD
Esa capacidad de respuesta funciona gracias a Jaspar, un asistente de inteligencia artificial integrado directamente en la experiencia.
Xavier Manzanares, director de jugabilidad de GenAI en Ubisoft, declaró a Variety que “los juegos de mañana escucharán, entenderán y reaccionarán a los jugadores mucho más de lo que lo hacen hoy”. El directivo agregó que la investigación de la compañía “ofrece un vistazo de lo que la jugabilidad adaptativa y generativa podría sumar sobre sistemas de juego ya probados”.
En mayo de 2026, Ubisoft confirmó que estaba acelerando sus inversiones en torno a Teammates, con aplicaciones de IA destinadas al control de calidad, personajes más inteligentes y mundos capaces de reaccionar en tiempo real al comportamiento del jugador.
PUBLICIDAD
El uso de IA en Ubisoft ya generó problemas
La incorporación de inteligencia artificial generativa a los desarrollos de Ubisoft no estuvo exenta de incidentes. Anno 117: Pax Romana fue uno de los juegos en los que se detectaron artefactos visuales atribuidos a IA generativa dentro del arte final del título. La compañía terminó retirando esas imágenes.
El registro de Motherbrain llega, además, en un año marcado por decisiones estructurales en la empresa. Ubisoft cerró cuatro estudios, canceló seis proyectos y eliminó unos 380 puestos de trabajo en los últimos meses, mientras su dirección compara públicamente el impacto de la IA generativa con el salto tecnológico del 2D al 3D en la industria de los videojuegos.
PUBLICIDAD
La apuesta de Ubisoft tampoco es un caso aislado dentro del sector. Capcom reconoció que utiliza inteligencia artificial generativa en sus desarrollos, una decisión que, según la compañía japonesa, permitirá reducir los períodos de producción de sus juegos.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Tesla necesita que sus trabajadores enseñen a Optimus a trabajar. El problema es que no todos quieren hacerlo
articles.text:
Hay una pregunta que la expansión de la inteligencia artificial está haciendo cada vez menos abstracta: ¿qué pensaríamos si nos pidieran entrenar una tecnología que algún día podría hacer nuestro trabajo? La situación ya ha aparecido, con matices distintos entre diferentes profesiones para enseñar a sistemas de IA cómo realizar determinadas tareas. Hasta ahora, buena parte de esa conversación había ocurrido dentro de una pantalla. Con los robots humanoides, esa misma tensión empieza a trasladarse también al mundo físico.
Eso es precisamente lo que ha ocurrido alrededor de Optimus. Según The Information, Tesla comunicó en enero a trabajadores de sus fábricas de Texas y California que quería que algunos utilizaran equipos capaces de registrar sus movimientos para enseñar al humanoide tareas del entorno de producción. Algunos se quejaron porque, de acuerdo con el medio, sabían que aquellos robots estaban diseñados para sustituir eventualmente trabajo humano. De pronto, enseñar a la máquina tenía una consecuencia mucho más fácil de visualizar.
Enseñar a Optimus cómo trabajamos
Lo que Tesla necesita recopilar no es simplemente vídeo de personas trabajando, sino ejemplos de cómo ejecutamos físicamente determinadas tareas. El aprendizaje por imitación permite utilizar demostraciones humanas como referencia para enseñar al robot movimientos y secuencias de acciones, y la propia compañía mantiene puestos específicos de recopilación de datos para Optimus en los que los empleados manipulan objetos, siguen recorridos establecidos y utilizan equipos de captura de movimiento mientras realizan acciones determinadas. Esa necesidad de ejemplos es uno de los grandes obstáculos de la robótica humanoide: conseguir que una máquina se desenvuelva en situaciones variadas exige reunir enormes cantidades de datos sobre comportamientos que para nosotros resultan naturales.
Las quejas de algunos trabajadores no hicieron desaparecer esa necesidad. The Information señala que Tesla empezó a contratar recopiladores de datos dedicados y a instalar cámaras en las fábricas para registrar tareas, mientras buena parte de ese trabajo se realizaba lejos de las líneas de producción activas. Durante el verano, la compañía comenzó además a establecer centros de entrenamiento en distintos puntos de Estados Unidos, incluidos Colorado, Arizona y Florida. Así que todo parece indicar que el método no desapareció: cambió progresivamente quién proporcionaba esos ejemplos y dónde se recopilaban.
Todo esto ocurre mientras Optimus sigue teniendo problemas bastante más básicos que aprender nuevas tareas. El medio señala que las manos y antebrazos reúnen más de un centenar de pequeños componentes, incluidos tornillos, que todavía requieren montaje manual, y algunas unidades recién fabricadas necesitan correcciones nada más salir de la línea. Los sensores táctiles también han dado problemas de fiabilidad, hasta el punto de que Tesla ha desarrollado una capa similar a un guante que puede sustituirse sin cambiar toda la mano. A ello se suma que el robot todavía requiere programación para ejecutar tareas concretas en entornos cuidadosamente controlados.
El caso del robot humanoide tiene además precedentes cada vez más reconocibles fuera de las fábricas. Hemos visto a guionistas, directores y productores de Hollywood aceptar trabajos para evaluar o generar material destinado a entrenar modelos de IA, mientras actores de voz se enfrentan a ofertas y contratos vinculados al desarrollo de réplicas sintéticas. En atención al cliente, trabajadores de Amazon también han expresado su preocupación por estar alimentando herramientas que podrían asumir parte de sus funciones. Este escenario tiene un punto en común: parte del conocimiento necesario para automatizar un trabajo sigue procediendo de las personas que ya saben hacerlo.
Musk ha situado Optimus entre las mayores apuestas de futuro de Tesla, pero la distancia entre esa ambición y el estado actual del proyecto sigue siendo considerable. La compañía habría alcanzado una producción de varios centenares de robots semanales y sus responsables quieren disponer antes de acabar 2026 de una línea automatizada continua capaz de producir más de 1.000 unidades por semana.

Ultra-configurable sans être véritablement haut de gamme, la Revolution X Pro pourrait occuper un entre-deux très intéressant sur le marché des manettes "pro". articles.title: Nvidia launches new AI safety program designed at stopping models escaping their sandboxes
articles.text:
Nvidia launches new AI safety program designed at stopping models escaping their sandboxes
Nvidia wants to control AI agents with hardware and software safeguards
- Nvidia response to "recent security incidents" by tightening restrictions on autonomous agents
- New software and hardware safeguards impose barriers if agents go rogue
- More than 100 customers have already agreed to work with the principles
Nvidia hasunveiled the new Open Agent Safety Platform designed to prevent autonomous AI agents from 'escaping' and acting beyond their established boundaries.
Following several recent alarming reports of AI-led attacks, the company admitted that safety should not just rely on safeguards built into AI models and applications, and that additional compute and hardware-level controls should also be used as more solid barriers.
"Recent security incidents have underscored the need to equip organizations with open, customizable tools," the company wrote in its announcement.
Nvidia adds even more layers of control for autonomous AI agents
The Open Agent Safety Platform consists of two key controls – OpenShell, which Nvidia describes as a software-based "secure runtime boundary," and Sentry, a hardware-based "watchdog" running on its BlueField-4 DPUs.
"Safety and security require full-stack engineering. NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform brings together industry, researchers and public-sector organizations to share best practices, align on evaluation methods and foster international cooperation," company CEO Jensen Huang summarized.
While existing model-level safety mechanisms are designed to tell AI not to behave in a certain way, the software-level OpenShell implements technical boundaries to actually prevent an agent from ignoring those instructions. Nvidia also argues that Sentry can quarantine and stop an AI agent within milliseconds.
Over 100 customers such as SpaceXAI, Anthropic and Microsoft are already using Nvidia's software and hardware-based safeguards.

The news, of course, comes after several high-profile instances where AI agents have operated beyond their intended controls, however while these new Nvidia-backed safeguards may be new, the overall principles aren't. The company is just stressing the importance of principles we're already familiar with, like least privilege, isolation/quarantining and detailed monitoring.
"As we continue to discover the frontier of AI capabilities, we must accelerate discovery at the frontier of AI safety," Huang added.
