articles.title: Reacher : Prime Video annonce déjà une saison 6 pour la série avec Alan Ritchson
articles.text:
Reacher : Prime Video annonce déjà une saison 6 pour la série avec Alan Ritchson
La série Reacher accumule les renouvellements cette année et décroche déjà une saison 6 alors que la saison 5 est seulement en tournage.
Jack Reacher n'a pas fini de mener l’enquête sur Prime Video. La plateforme de streaming d'Amazon vient en effet d'annoncer que la série tirée des romans de Lee Child va avoir droit à une saison 6, 12 jours seulement après la fin de la diffusion de la saison 4 et alors que la saison 5, annoncée il y a quelques mois, est actuellement en tournage.
Rien n'arrête Reacher
Prime Video n'a pas de temps à perdre : Reacher étant une série très populaire sur le service de streaming (la saison 4 a réuni 66 millions de téléspectateurs en 28 jours et les saisons 2 et 4 figurent parmi les plus plus vues sur la plateforme), prévoir ses futures saisons longtemps à l'avance permet de maintenir le rythme d'une nouvelle saison par an.
Ainsi, la saison 5 était déjà quasiment écrite quand la plateforme l'a officialisé en mai dernier, et son tournage a pu commencer en juillet, juste avant le début de diffusion de la saison 4.
Cette saison 5 est basée sur le roman Bienvenue à Mother’s Rest, 20e opus de la saga de Lee Child, mais on ne sait pas encore quelle histoire la saison 6 adaptera.
"Reacher frappe fort," a déclaré Peter Friedlander, directeur de la télévision internationale chez Amazon MGM Studios. "Ce que Lee Child a imaginé, et ce à quoi Nick Santora et ses équipes créatives ont donné vie, est tout simplement incroyable. Alan Ritchson est Jack Reacher : il a livré une performance qui a captivé le public du monde entier."
"Avec nos partenaires de Paramount Television Studios, nous sommes ravis de poursuivre cette aventure," a ajouté Friedlander. "Reacher est une série véritablement emblématique, et nous sommes enchantés de continuer l'aventure aux côtés de cette équipe artistique et technique exceptionnelle pour une sixième saison."
Reacher est une série si populaire qu'elle a récemment donné naissance à un spin-off, Neagley, qui connaît lui aussi un joli succès sur Prime Video et pourrait bientôt faire également l'objet d'un renouvellement.

articles.title: Custom ChatGPTs push ClickFix attacks to deploy RAT malware
articles.text:
Custom variants of OpenAI’s ChatGPT promoted in sponsored Google results are directing unsuspecting users to malicious sites that use ClickFix attacks to deliver malware.
The threat actor is abusing the legitimate feature in the AI platform that lets users create a version of ChatGPT tailored for a specific task that combines instructions, extra knowledge, and skills.
OpenAI hosts these custom GPTs, which can be published for others to install and use. The company plans to retire custom GPTs on December 11.
The malicious campaign was identified by Huntress, a managed detection and response (MDR) company, whose researchers say it affected dozens of users.
The threat actor named the malicious GPT model 'Plus 5.6' and configured it to direct users to an alleged backup site hosted on Google Sites.
However, the page shows a fake Cloudflare check and instructs visitors to run a PowerShell command, which deploys the infection chain.
Huntress researchers observed similar attacks in the past, which used deceptive ChatGPT conversations to launch ClickFix ruses and compromise targets, but using custom GPTs is a novel approach.
In both attacks, the malicious instructions are hosted on the legitimate ChatGPT.com domain, lending legitimacy to the operation and increasing the chances the victim will follow the instructions.
If executed locally, the provided PowerShell command installs a malicious MSI that launches a legitimate, signed application and a modified DLL loading the malware.
The payload used in this campaign is a remote access trojan (RAT) with capabilities for remote desktop access, audio and camera capture, file searches, host reconnaissance, and running additional payloads.
For persistence, the malware creates a new Run key in the Windows Registry and also a scheduled task, both named ‘Canon Configuration Reader.’
Huntress says it investigated at least 40 incidents connecting to the Google Sites page but confirmed that only two involved a custom GPT variant.
OpenAI took down the first GPT by September 25. Two days later, on September 27, the researchers found a second GPT linked to the same campaign, which was still active when they published their report.
More recent attacks switched from a Canon-signed host application to a Stardock-signed one and changed how it concealed and delivered the loader, although the payload remained the same.
From the multi-stage attack chain, Huntress highlights phase 6, noting that the attackers built a custom encrypted file system to conceal the persistence script and RAT.
“Instead of one encrypted blob, it's a custom archive with its own folder tree, basically a homemade, encrypted zip file,” researchers say.
“It starts with a small header, followed by an index of 1,128 entries (one per file or folder, each recording its parent, its size and a per-file key), and then the file contents, packed back to back.”
Huntress says that most of the infection chain runs in memory or is supported by files that appear benign. This allows defenders to implement detections based on process activity monitoring.
The researchers provide a set of "detection opportunities" that include PowerShell pinging msiexec.exe to silently launch an MSI installer from the temporary folder.
Additional signs of compromise refer to a signed app starting from an unusual folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\, and a matching Run value and scheduled task that reappear if deleted.

articles.title: Le ray tracing fait exploser les configurations requises pour le remaster de The Witcher 3
articles.text:
Geralt de Riv nous revient – encore une fois – avec un traitement graphique qui se veut flatteur… enfin, sauf pour notre porte-monnaie.
Le geste est rare, presque inédit. En effet, à seulement quelques heures de la publication de son nouveau jeu, le studio CD Projekt RED détaille les exigences techniques de The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered. On peut dire que le petit a bien poussé !
Sortie prévue… aujourd'hui même !
En août dernier, à l'occasion de la Gamescom de Cologne, les Polonais de CD Projekt RED levaient le voile sur deux nouveautés autour de The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, sans aucun doute leur jeu le plus populaire.
Dans le courant de l'année 2027, une nouvelle – la troisième – extension doit voir le jour, Songs of the Past. Mais, bien avant cela et comme pour préparer le terrain, une mise à jour majeure était évoquée, un vrai « remaster ». L'objectif est d'aboutir à une refonte complète du rendu du jeu avec l'introduction du path tracing, une gestion plus réaliste des éclairages et de nombreux apports tant au niveau de la végétation que des chevelures des personnages.
Pour ce faire, le moteur graphique du jeu évolue lui aussi avec un passage au DirectX 12 natif. Il faut dire que The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt accuse le poids des ans : il est à l'origine sorti en 2015 et de l'eau a coulé sous les ponts. Reste qu'à côté de toutes ces annonces, CD Projekt RED semblait éviter la question qui fâche : celle des exigences matérielles.
Attention, les exigences matérielles bondissent
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered doit sortir aujourd'hui même et nous avons enfin des précisions sur ces fameuses configurations requises. Le fait est que plus de dix ans après la sortie du jeu originel, elles ont bien changé.
Configuration « minimum » :
- Système d'exploitation : Windows 11 64-bit
- Processeur : Intel Core i5-8400 ou AMD Ryzen 5 2600
- Mémoire vive : 12 Go
- Carte graphique : NVIDIA GTX 1660 ou AMD Radeon RX 5500 ou Intel Arc A580
- Mémoire vidéo : 6 Go
- Espace disque : 60 Go, SSD
Ce minimum requis est donné pour jouer en Full HD (1080p) à 30 images par seconde avec les détails graphiques sur « low » avec une précision subtile : la GeForce GTX 1660 doit permettre d'atteindre les 60 ips.
Configuration « recommandée » :
- Système d'exploitation : Windows 11 64-bit
- Processeur : Intel Core i7-8700K ou AMD Ryzen 5 3600X
- Mémoire vive : 16 Go
- Carte graphique : NVIDIA RTX 2060 S ou AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT ou Intel Arc B580
- Mémoire vidéo : 8 Go
- Espace disque : 60 Go, SSD
Nous restons ici en Full HD (1080p), mais à 60 images par seconde et avec des détails graphiques sur « high ».
Configuration « ultra » :
- Système d'exploitation : Windows 11 64-bit
- Processeur : Intel Core i7-13700K ou AMD Ryzen 7 7700X
- Mémoire vive : 24 Go
- Carte graphique : NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti ou AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT ou Intel Arc B580 (XeSS)
- Mémoire vidéo : 12 Go
- Espace disque : 60 Go, SSD
Avec cette troisième configuration, nous quittons enfin le Full HD pour du 1440p avec, logique, les détails graphiques sur « ultra ». CD Projekt RED vise encore le 60 images par seconde. Notez que pour continuer à utiliser une carte graphique Intel Arc B580, l'activation de XeSS est indispensable.
Configuration « RT minimum » :
- Système d'exploitation : Windows 11 64-bit
- Processeur : Intel Core i7-11700K ou AMD Ryzen 7 5800X
- Mémoire vive : 16 Go
- Carte graphique : NVIDIA RTX 2060 ou AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT ou Intel Arc B580
- Mémoire vidéo : 8 Go
- Espace disque : 60 Go, SSD
Première configuration avec activation du ray tracing, cette machine impose l'utilisation des techniques de mise à l'échelle sur toutes les plateformes (DLSS, FSR, XeSS). La configuration est donnée pour jouer en Full HD (1080p) avec les détails graphiques sur « RT », mais à seulement 30 ips.
Configuration « RT recommandée » :
- Système d'exploitation : Windows 11 64-bit
- Processeur : Intel Core i7-13700K ou AMD Ryzen 7 7700X
- Mémoire vive : 24 Go
- Carte graphique : NVIDIA RTX 4080 ou AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
- Mémoire vidéo : 12 Go
- Espace disque : 60 Go, SSD
Ray tracing toujours, mais cette fois pour jouer en 1440p et avec une vitesse d'animation à 60 ips. Cette configuration délaisse les solutions graphiques Intel, aucune Arc n'étant suffisamment puissante à en croire CD Projekt RED.
Configuration « path tracing » :
- Système d'exploitation : Windows 11 64-bit
- Processeur : Intel Core i9-13900K ou AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- Mémoire vive : 24 Go
- Carte graphique : NVIDIA RTX 5080
- Mémoire vidéo : 16 Go
- Espace disque : 60 Go, SSD
Ultime configuration présentée, celle-ci permet logiquement de pousser tous les potards au maximum tout en conservant une vitesse d'animation de 60 ips tout en montant jusqu'en 4K. Attention cependant, il faut activer DLSS et sa génération d'images. Enfin, notez qu'en dehors d'au moins une GeForce RTX 5080, point de salut ! The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered est bel et bien considérablement plus lourd que le jeu originel.

articles.title: Après un vol test calamiteux, la Nasa veut quand même refaire voler des astronautes dans le Starliner d'ici 2028
articles.text:
On aurait pu croire, initialement, à la fin du Starliner. En juillet, l’inspection générale de l’agence spatiale américaine publiait un rapport reprochant à la Nasa d’avoir trop fait confiance à Boeing et pas assez testé sa capsule. On pouvait alors se demander si ce programme n’allait pas en rester là, surtout avec la fin de plus en plus proche de l’ISS.
Pourtant, dans un communiqué publié ce lundi 28 septembre, le patron de la Nasa, Jared Isaacman, envisage un autre destin pour le Starliner. De toute évidence, l’agence veut toujours un deuxième véhicule habité pour ses astronautes, en plus du Crew Dragon de SpaceX – le seul, côté américain, à assurer les rotations vers la Station spatiale internationale.
Vu l’historique de la capsule, la décision peut étonner.
En juin 2024, le premier vol test habité de Starliner devait durer huit jours. Or, des fuites d’hélium et des propulseurs en panne ont poussé la Nasa à faire revenir la capsule vide. Ses deux passagers, Butch Wilmore et Suni Williams, ont été rapatriés dans une capsule SpaceX, après plus de neuf mois en orbite et beaucoup d’hésitation.
En février dernier, la Nasa a publié le rapport de son équipe d’enquête interne, qui compte 61 recommandations.
Le rapport visait surtout les petits propulseurs du module de service, ceux qui orientent la capsule. On les avait fait fonctionner hors des conditions pour lesquelles ils avaient été qualifiés. Les essais au sol ont mis en cause plusieurs facteurs, dont la chaleur autour de ces propulseurs et certaines caractéristiques de leur conception. Boeing a depuis modifié la gestion thermique de ce module.
Mais la Nasa avait quand même classé l’incident au niveau des désastres Challenger et Columbia, en « accident de type A », une catégorie qui couvre notamment la perte de contrôle d’un véhicule ou la perte de vies humaines.
Un vol à vide d’abord, des astronautes en 2028
Pour vérifier ces corrections, Starliner-1 partira vers l’ISS sans personne à bord, au plus tôt en décembre 2026, sinon en janvier 2027.
Ce vol doit montrer que les propulseurs tiennent la température et fournir les données requises pour certifier la capsule. Ensuite, Boeing modifiera les vannes des propulseurs : leur joint se déforme, ce qui perturbe la poussée. Aussi au programme : le renouvellement des batteries et des propulseurs sur le module d’équipage, et des parachutes retouchés.
Si tout se passe bien, Starliner-2 emmènera des astronautes « d’ici 2028 », d’après Isaacman, qui a aussi annoncé que l’astronaute Woody Hoburg commandera cette mission. Lors de la conférence de presse, rapportée par CNN, la Nasa a chiffré la rallonge à 359 millions de dollars (environ 315 millions d’euros), pour ces améliorations et pour certifier un nouveau lanceur, la fusée Vulcan.
Dans ce processus, Starliner doit aussi changer de lanceur : l’Atlas V de United Launch Alliance (ULA, l’entreprise commune de Boeing et Lockheed Martin) vit ses derniers vols. La Nasa veut donc autoriser la Vulcan, la fusée qui la remplace, à transporter des équipages. Là encore, cela nécessite de passer par la case de la certification.
Tout cela doit se faire dans un calendrier serré : la Nasa prévoit d’exploiter l’ISS jusqu’en 2030. Si Starliner-2 décolle en 2028, il ne restera que deux à trois ans pour assurer les vols habités prévus vers la station. Cela étant, il y a aussi l’après-ISS. Isaacman veut d’ailleurs faire voler le Starliner vers les futures stations spatiales commerciales, en plus du Crew Dragon.

articles.title: Microsoft 365: Optionales Update deinstalliert Programme, statt alte zu aktualisieren
articles.text:
Microsoft 365: Optionales Update deinstalliert Programme, statt alte zu aktualisieren
Bei Updates für Microsoft-Produkte wie Windows kommt es immer wieder einmal zu Problemen. Für Aufsehen sorgte etwa der sogenannte Patch Tuesday vom 13. Januar 2026. Statt wie geplant kritische Sicherheitslücken zu schließen, brachte das Update selbst zusätzliche Probleme mit. Microsoft musste mit Notfall-Updates gegensteuern.
Lizenzen aufgehoben, Programme deinstalliert
Jetzt steht Microsoft 365 im Mittelpunkt eines Update-Problems. Mit dem optionalen Update KB5002907 für den Microsoft-Dienst sollten eigentlich Microsoft-365-Apps aktualisiert werden, die mehr als 90 Tage veraltet waren oder nicht mehr ordnungsgemäß aktualisiert wurden. Stattdessen sollen bestehende Lizenzen aufgehoben worden sein, wie Golem berichtet. Zum Teil verschwanden die betreffenden Programme auch einfach.
Der Konzern musste daher einmal mehr nachjustieren. Aufgrund von „unerwarteten Ergebnissen auf einigen Geräten“ habe Microsoft die Verteilung des Updates vorübergehend gestoppt, wie es in einer Mitteilung heißt. Betroffen sollen Computer sein, auf denen Office 2016 und Office 2019 läuft.
Microsoft 365: Update als Reparaturaktion
Das als „Reparaturaktion“ bezeichnete Update sollte laut Microsoft neben der Aktualisierungsoption den Wechsel zu einem aktuellen Build der Microsoft-365-Apps ermöglichen.
Gestartet hatte Microsoft die Verteilung des Updates Ende September 2026. Es stand für Geräte mit Windows 11, Windows 10, Windows Server 2025, Windows Server 2022 und Windows Server 2019 bereit. Es galt für Geräte, die den aktuellen Kanal oder den monatlichen Enterprise-Kanal verwenden. Weil es sich um ein optionales Update handelte, gab es aber keine automatische Installation.
Produkt erneut aktivieren oder neu installieren
Microsoft rät betroffenen Nutzer:innen jetzt, das Produkt erneut zu aktivieren beziehungsweise neu zu installieren. Sollte das nicht funktionieren, bittet Microsoft darum, den Support zu kontaktieren. Ob und wann Microsoft ein repariertes Update bereitstellt, ist nicht bekannt.

articles.title: Spaces : OpenAI s'attaque à Notion et Google Docs depuis ChatGPT — Frandroid
articles.text:
Tout le monde va parler de Dots. Mais ce qui m’a marqué lors de la keynote OpenAI, c’était Spaces.
Tout le monde attendait dots, les agents toujours actifs d’OpenAI, et Sam Altman a enchaîné sans respirer : « presque tous les logiciels de productivité n’ont pas été conçus pour que l’IA et les humains travaillent bien ensemble. Nous changeons ça aussi ». Derrière la formule, un produit qui ressemble furieusement à Notion, et qui est livré dès aujourd’hui.
Spaces commence par une page. On y écrit un plan, on y fait des recherches, on y génère des images ou des données, on y construit quelque chose.
Une touche « / » ouvre la liste de ce que l’on peut insérer : graphiques interactifs, feuilles de calcul, prototypes fonctionnels. Les pages et les fichiers vivent ensemble dans un espace, comme dans un Drive, avec une différence de taille : on tague un collègue ou son dot dans un commentaire, et l’agent se met au travail directement dans la page.
Une page peut aussi recevoir une consigne permanente, comme « surveille tel canal Slack et mets-toi à jour chaque jour », et un graphique peut se rafraîchir toutes les heures sans qu’on y touche. L’outil évoluera rapidement, des présentations « lisibles et modifiables par les agents » arriveront « bientôt ».
En attendant, Spaces est disponible aujourd’hui pour les abonnés ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium et Enterprise.
Ce qu’on a vu sur scène
La démo de Holly, de l’équipe produit d’OpenAI, tournait autour d’une fausse application musicale.
Une page rassemblait les retours des testeurs de la veille. Elle a tagué son dot pour transformer un tableau en histogramme, filtré les données par type de retour, puis demandé d’ajouter une FAQ et « la stat sur l’onboarding que cet ingénieur m’a envoyée en message privé sur Slack ».
L’agent est allé la chercher. C’est la vraie nouveauté par rapport à un Google Doc ou à Canvas, la zone d’édition que ChatGPT propose depuis fin 2024 : le document a accès à tout ce que vous avez connecté à votre compte, pas seulement à ce qui est écrit dedans. Ce qu’on n’a pas vu compte tout autant. Rien sur l’historique des versions, sur les permissions fines, sur l’export, sur le mobile ou sur ce qui se passe quand deux personnes et deux dots modifient le même paragraphe. Et une page « vivante » qui se met à jour seule, c’est aussi une page qui change quand personne ne regarde. Reste à savoir qui valide.
Malheureusement, pour l’Europe, dots est exclu au lancement, OpenAI n’a rien précisé pour Spaces, lancé le même jour, et on partirait plutôt sur la même réponse.

articles.title: Former EVGA manager reveals how Nvidia's Founders Edition cards helped drive the company out of GPUs
articles.text:
Winners & losers: EVGA's 2022 exit from Nvidia graphics cards remains one of the industry's most striking partner breakups, and this first-hand account shows how the relationship worked day to day. Hedrick describes a company squeezed by Nvidia's Founders Edition cards, pressure to keep a loss-making entry model and tight control over launch information, all in a business that made up 78% of EVGA's sales. It's only one side of the story, though. Nvidia's CEO and outside reports point to EVGA's own strategy and costs.
EVGA announced in 2022 that it would stop making Nvidia graphics cards, blaming the decision on what it described as an abusive relationship. Now, former EVGA Product Manager Brendon Ray Hedrick has shed more light on why that happened, including having to compete against Nvidia's own Founders Edition cards.
In a lengthy personal account, Hedrick, who worked at EVGA between 2016 and 2019, recalls the concern when Nvidia introduced its Pascal Founders Edition cards: the company supplying EVGA's chips was increasingly competing for the same customers.
According to Hedrick, EVGA needed a model at Nvidia's advertised starting price, even if it lost money. Failing to offer one could jeopardize GPU allocations, though he says identifying the reason for a reduction was difficult.
"We needed to keep a loss leader – a card we sold at a loss – to keep Nvidia happy and protect our access to the chips," he writes.
That left pricier custom cards to generate profits. But as Nvidia improved its designs and automatic clock management, Hedrick says spending more on EVGA's circuitry and cooling delivered increasingly modest gaming gains. The cheaper models, meanwhile, were frequently sold out.
There were also issues with launch preparations. Hedrick recalls learning GTX and RTX specifications at the same time as the public. "Nvidia was fiercely protective of its announcements, and I remember how angry it could become with partners over information that leaked before an official reveal," he said.
To catch the culprits, different colored dots were used on retailer images to trace leaks. "If an image leaked and Nvidia came back to us, we could identify which retailer had originally received that image set," Hedrick explains.
By September 2022, the financial squeeze had reached a tipping point. As reported when EVGA announced its departure, the company said it was losing hundreds of dollars on RTX 3080 and RTX 3090 cards following price cuts. It also complained about discovering final suggested prices at Nvidia's public announcements and having limited freedom to set its own.
At the time, CEO Andrew Han insisted the move was about principle rather than money, following unsuccessful attempts to renegotiate the partnership.
The decision meant abandoning a business that accounted for 78% of EVGA's sales. EVGA nevertheless ruled out making AMD or Intel cards, expanding into new product categories, or selling the company. It said existing graphics card owners would retain warranty support.
But there was another side to the story. An Igor's Lab report blamed some of EVGA's margin problems on outsourcing circuit boards and coolers. It estimated EVGA's margins at around 5%, against roughly 10% for competing manufacturers. Longer warranties and the Step-Up upgrade program also added costs.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had his own explanation for the split. He claimed EVGA boss Andrew Han had wanted to wind down the business for several years. Huang praised the partnership and suggested Han was ready to pursue something else.
"Andrew and EVGA are great partners, and were great partners, and I'm sad to see them leave the market," Huang said.

articles.title: OpenAI CEO Announces New AI Agent and Avoids Mention of Security Concerns at Developer Conference
articles.text:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman introduced a “remarkably capable, always-on” artificial intelligence agent at an appearance Tuesday where he avoided any reference to security concerns around the company’s most advanced models.
At the company’s annual developer conference, Altman made a slew of product announcements and updates, including the company’s new agents, called Dots. The agents, designed to complete ongoing tasks proactively on behalf of users, are a competitor of Meta’s personal agent Muse, which exploded in popularity after Meta’s own conference last week.
Dot agents will be “like an AI helper that always has your back, inspired by the cool versions of what we all watched in movies growing up,” Altman said.
On Monday, OpenAI said it was holding off on the release of a new AI model out of security concerns voiced by its researchers. The disclosure followed broader calls within the industry to decelerate the pace of the technology’s advance to let safety measures catch up.
In his remarks on stage, Altman did not address the scrapped model, but he did offer some parting words about how the AI boom should be considered more like a period of renaissance than an industrial revolution.
“The best version of AI is not about making people cogs in a giant machine, ever whirring faster and faster. There are some parts of life that we cannot and should not automate,” Altman said. “AI should be about giving people more power over their own lives, more tools to create, learn, discover, expand knowledge.”
The company also announced the release of GPT-6.1 Sol, an upgraded version of its model GPT-6 Sol, and a premium speed tier called “Ultrafast,” among other launches and updates.
OpenAI’s announcements came as Altman’s industry peers were meeting with President Donald Trump Tuesday. While many in Silicon Valley have called for the government to help establish guardrails for the technology, Trump has pushed back against the idea of greater government oversight of AI.
While Altman was not in attendance because of the conference, OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman was at the White House, along with Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Amazon chief Jeff Bezos, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Tesla and SpaceX’s Elon Musk and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Several other industry leaders joined them, along with senior administration officials and House Speaker Mike Johnson.

articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO pitch includes a warning about human extinction
articles.text:
Anthropic has formally warned investors that its technology may pose “existential risks to humanity” in a long-awaited initial public offering prospectus circulated with a small group of partners in recent days.
The nearly $1 trillion AI start-up led by Dario Amodei devoted almost a third of its lengthy S-1 filing to detailing “risk factors,” including the potential of increasingly advanced AI models to manipulate, blackmail, and exhibit other unpredictable behaviors.
Anthropic outlined more prosaic risks, including the extreme concentration of its customer base, with close to a quarter of revenue last year coming from just two clients, according to people familiar with the filing.
The extraordinary warnings in its risk disclosures add to the challenge faced by public market investors in valuing the leading US AI group when it launches what is expected to be the most highly valued IPO of all time.
The Claude maker also provided investors with a clearer picture of the challenging economics of building state-of-the-art AI models ahead of the listing, expected on the Nasdaq this autumn.
Anthropic said it planned to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations in the coming years to support its rapid growth.
The AI lab’s backers are confident Anthropic can list at a valuation of more than $2 trillion, more than double the level achieved in its last funding round in May and beyond the $1.78 trillion achieved by Elon Musk’s SpaceX in June. They point to its extraordinary growth rate to justify their bullishness.

articles.title: Rockstar estaría preparando una nueva entrega de L.A. Noire después de publicar GTA 6: esto se conoce
articles.text:
Un rumor apunta a que Rockstar podría desarrollar una secuela del videojuego L.A. Noire después del lanzamiento de GTA 6. La información procede de un usuario de GTAForums y no fue confirmada por la compañía.
Según esa versión, el supuesto L.A. Noire 2 estaría ambientado en San Francisco durante los crímenes de Zodiac. El proyecto se encontraría en una etapa inicial de desarrollo y no llegaría antes de 2030, siempre de acuerdo con esa filtración.
PUBLICIDAD
El mismo informante sostuvo que el juego podría utilizar una tecnología de escaneado facial más avanzada, con la intención de llevar el realismo de las animaciones a un nuevo nivel. Sin embargo, no se conocieron posibles plataformas ni otros detalles sobre su producción.
Qué se sabe sobre el supuesto proyecto
La filtración ganó atención porque el usuario, identificado como Shahanshah, habría anticipado hace tres años algunos elementos relacionados con GTA 6, entre ellos detalles sobre los personajes Lucía y Jason.
Aun así, no existe un anuncio oficial de Rockstar Games sobre una continuación de L.A. Noire. Por ese motivo, los datos sobre su ambientación, su tecnología y una posible fecha de lanzamiento deben considerarse especulativos.
PUBLICIDAD
L.A. Noire fue editado en 2011 para PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 y PC. El juego, desarrollado por Team Bondi, combinó mundo abierto e investigaciones basadas en interrogatorios y animaciones faciales para detectar pistas en las reacciones de los sospechosos.
La obra recibió una remasterización en 2017 para PlayStation 4, Xbox One y Nintendo Switch. Desde entonces, circularon versiones sobre una secuela, aunque Rockstar no confirmó nuevos proyectos vinculados con esa franquicia.
Cuándo sale GTA 6
GTA 6 saldrá el 19 de noviembre de 2026, según confirmó Rockstar Games. El lanzamiento está previsto para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, por lo que los jugadores de PC deberán esperar: la compañía todavía no anunció una versión para esa plataforma. La fecha corresponde a un retraso informado por el estudio en noviembre de 2025.
PUBLICIDAD
Rockstar indicó que las reservas digitales permitirán precargarlo desde el 12 de noviembre de 2026.
La edición estándar de Grand Theft Auto VI costará USD 79,99, mientras que la versión Ultimate tendrá un precio de USD 99,99.
Grand Theft Auto VI tendrá como protagonistas a Jason y Lucía y transcurrirá en Leonida, con Vice City entre sus escenarios. Esa es la fecha vigente, salvo cambios.
De momento, Rockstar Games ni Take-Two Interactive han confirmado la llegada del juego para PC.
De qué trata GTA 6
Grand Theft Auto VI es un juego de acción y mundo abierto que sigue a Jason y Lucia, una pareja atrapada en una conspiración criminal que se extiende por Leonida, el estado ficticio donde transcurre la historia.
PUBLICIDAD
Según Rockstar Games, los protagonistas siempre supieron que las cartas estaban en su contra.
Sin embargo, un golpe que parecía sencillo sale mal y los obliga a apoyarse mutuamente mientras recorren “el lado más oscuro del lugar más soleado de Estados Unidos”. La trama se centrará en su relación y en los riesgos que enfrentan dentro del submundo criminal.
La acción volverá a Vice City, una versión contemporánea de la ciudad inspirada en Miami, aunque el mapa también incluirá otras zonas de Leonida. Rockstar mostró ambientes urbanos, playas, carreteras, pantanos, cayos e instalaciones industriales, lo que anticipa una experiencia con escenarios variados.
PUBLICIDAD
El juego permitirá controlar a Jason y Lucia durante la aventura. Los avances oficiales muestran robos, persecuciones, tiroteos y actividades vinculadas con la vida cotidiana de ambos personajes.
Rockstar todavía no reveló todos los detalles de las misiones, la progresión ni sus modos adicionales, por lo que parte de la experiencia permanece bajo reserva.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Accel and Google back Dodge AI's ambitions to automate enterprise software maintenance with agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Accel and Google back Dodge AI’s ambitions to automate enterprise software maintenance with agents
A startup called Dodge AI Inc. closed on $2.65 million in seed funding today, saying it can help large organizations avoid hiring an army of external consultants to keep their enterprise software up and running.
Today’s round was co-led by Accel and the Google AI Futures Fund and saw participation from Schema Ventures, New Build Ventures, Antler and a number of angel investors from SAP SE’s ecosystem, the startup said.
Dodge AI says it’s trying to disrupt a $600 billion “enterprise firefighting” industry that has emerged specifically to maintain corporate software platforms such as SAP and Salesforce. These incredibly complex platforms form the backbone of most large enterprises today, and they require extensive upkeep to ensure everything is working properly to keep businesses up and running. Indeed, running enterprise software is an endless task, and installing it in the first place is only the beginning.
The thing to understand is that every enterprise platform is different. An organization might begin with a basic Salesforce deployment, but over the years it will evolve that platform with thousands of custom rules, company-specific configurations and workarounds, adapting it to its particular needs. This is why most organizations end up hiring large systems integrators such as Accenture Plc or IBM Corp., which assign teams of anywhere between 20 to 50 people to work specifically on their deployment, handling support tickets, upgrades and everyday operations.
Dodge AI co-founder and Chief Executive Rebhav Bharadwaj doesn’t argue that this model has failed, but says it’s not the most efficient way of doing things. Over the years, hundreds of fixes may go undocumented, while the customizations pile up and technical debt compounds over time, he explained.
After a few years, most companies find themselves utterly reliant on the systems integrator they hired to help them understand and operate their own software. “For a long time, the only way to maintain enterprise systems was to add more people,” Bharadwaj said.
But that’s no longer the case, he says. Bharadwaj’s startup has developed a “control plane” for enterprise software maintenance that’s controlled by artificial intelligence agents. It’s designed to be overlaid across systems such as SAP, Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics, so that the agents can analyze the deployment, get to grips with all of the customizations and configurations and so on. The aim is to automate maintenance going forward.
According to Bharadwaj, it’s capable of identifying the root cause of system failures, recommending and implementing fixes, and generally handling maintenance issues faster than any human team can do. Most importantly, Dodge AI documents all of the changes, exceptions and custom logic that’s implemented, helping organizations to actually understand their information technology infrastructure.
“Dodge AI gives enterprises the ability to continuously improve and heal their mission-critical systems so incidents can be resolved faster, technical debt can be understood and the knowledge trapped inside maintenance work can become the foundation for future transformation,” Bharadwaj said.
At its core, Dodge AI understands enterprise software installations by creating what it calls an “exception intelligence context graph,” which connects all of the business processes, enterprise resource planning configurations and legacy systems. Bharadwaj said that these exceptions are the key, as they explain why separate warehouses may allocate inventory differently, for example, or why one pricing rule overrides another. Dodge AI’s agents work to capture and document all of this logic and build a centralized source of truth that guides their maintenance work.
The startup claims it has already convinced several large enterprises to drop their human consultants and hand over the reins to its AI agents. It’s not naming these customers, but said it’s already handling hundreds of queries per hour, helping them to resolve issues that would normally take several hours, if not days to fix, within minutes.
For instance, it helped one customer to figure out that a warehouse loading failure was caused by an incorrect Goods Receipt Note within multiple systems and fixed the problem in a matter of minutes. In another example, it helped one of its customers optimize a SAP inventory planning process that was continuously crashing, making it 132 times faster than before.
Moving forward, Dodge AI wants to do more than just help enterprises to maintain their software. It also has its sights set on helping companies to accelerate their digital transformations. Many organizations want to modernize but are scared to move forward because they’re worried about breaking their most critical systems and applications. Bharadwaj believes that understanding the custom logic is key to preventing this from happening.
Accel investor Prayank Swaroop said application maintenance is one of the largest yet least modernized segments of the enterprise technology industry. “Dodge AI is taking on the work that keeps the world’s most important systems running every day,” he said. “By starting with maintenance, the team is building the context layer enterprises need before agents can safely operate in production.”

articles.title: Canadians spend 80 hours per year deciding what to watch: Roku
articles.text:
A new report from Roku has revealed new data on Canadians’ streaming habits.
In its seventh annual VOD Evolution Study, the streaming company found that Canadians spend a total of about 80 hours per year figuring out what to watch. A key reason for this, the study found, is that 59 per cent of people who stream TV said it’s hard to find something to watch because there are so many streaming services on the market. (On average, Canadians use four different streaming services, per Roku.)
Further, 60 per cent of people said they sometimes forget where to even stream a given movie or TV series. All of this comes as roughly 27 million Canadians now stream TV, a 35 per cent increase from five years ago, per Roku.
To address these kinds of issues, 65 per cent of respondents said they think ads would help them find a movie or TV show. On top of that, more than two-thirds of Canadians said they like ads to remind them when a movie or TV show they want to watch is available to stream. Thirty-five per cent of people also said that a TV home screen ad would feel less intrusive than traditional TV commercials.
According to Roku, 67 per cent of Canadians who stream take measurable action after seeing TV ads; 31 per cent search
for more info, 28 per cent visit a brand’s website, 19 per cent map look up the brand in-store, and 15 per cent scan a TV QR code.
Of course, Roku wants to promote its own curation tools here as a platform that features many streaming services within it. Some of these include free ad-supported television (FAST), which Roku notes is an option that continues to grow in popularity. Per the latest VOD Evolution Study, 84 per cent of Canadians watch ad-supported TV monthly with an average of 13 hours per week spent on these platforms, or about half of their total TV viewing.
To conduct this latest VOD Evolution Study on Roku’s behalf, Fuse Insights surveyed 2,043 Canadian adults in English and French in June 2026.

articles.title: Here's why OpenAI is absent from Nvidia's industry-wide effort to end rogue AI agents | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When Nvidia announced on Monday a new consortium of more than 100 companies dedicated to solving rogue AI agents, there was one name notably missing: OpenAI.
While OpenAI wasn’t the only big tech player that didn’t sign on — Amazon, Google, and Apple haven’t joined either — it was the most obvious missing player, especially because Anthropic is a supporter.
However, despite OpenAI’s lack of a public pledge to the consortium, which presumably means that each company will use and sell some version of the technology and contribute features back to the project, an OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that the company is supportive of Nvidia’s work.
The new effort, dubbed Nvidia’s Open Agent Safety Platform, is Nvidia’s attempt to spread its homegrown, and largely open source AI agent-security tech throughout the AI ecosystem as a direct response to the types of ongoing rogue AI agent incidents frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have disclosed.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been calling rogue AIs an ordinary engineering problem that can be solved like any other tech issue. The Open Agent Safety Platform is Huang putting his money where his mouth is.
OpenAI is working with Nvidia on agent security, including on one of the key bits of software that’s part of this platform: OpenShell. OpenShell is open sourced software that creates a sandbox specifically designed to keep agents from escaping.
While it is still curious that OpenAI didn’t simply become a supporter of the initiative like its archrival Anthropic did, the fact that frontier AI lab is supporting the effort is good news.
That’s because OpenAI, in particular, could benefit from this tech, at least according to Hugging Face founder and CEO Clem Delangue (who just sold his company to Nvidia for $12.9 billion earlier this month).
“From what we know (take with a grain of salt, we need much more transparency!), if @OpenAI had been running this on their own agents that attacked us, they would have caught them before we did!” Delangue posted.
Delangue said Hugging Face has already contributed a feature to the Open Agent Safety Platform that will detect and shut down AI agents that are using websites they are allowed to visit but are doing so in unauthorized ways. For instance, this feature will act if agents are bypassing their guardrails and coordinating an attack by writing notes to one another in an open source code hosting repository.
That’s one of the ways OpenAI said its wayward swarm of agents coordinated its attack on Hugging Face.
But there’s another reason why some of these big names, including OpenAI, might not want to publicly commit to Nvidia’s efforts. To use the full system, there is a hardware component that is not open source software, remains proprietary, and can only be deployed on Nvidia’s hardware.
The Open Agent Safety Platform doesn’t just offer a sandbox. It also enforces agent behavior at a hardware layer, where agents can’t detect that they are being watched. (Some AI models and agents lie and pretend to be following the rules when they know they are being watched.)
The hardware monitoring part relies on Nvidia Sentry, a proprietary feature that runs on special Nvidia processors called BlueField-4 data processing units. Sentry continuously monitors agent behavior from these processors and can instantly shut agents down, Nvidia promises.
While a hardware solution is clearly a good idea, it means that the Open Agent Safety Platform isn’t exactly a pure open source play. It allows Nvidia to ensure that this solution always runs best on its own hardware. Indeed, Nvidia has said that, for those already running workloads on its latest hardware, implementing the Open Agent Safety Platform is an easy software update.
Still, Nvidia competitors, including Arm and Intel, have signed on as Open Agent Safety Platform supporters because the sandbox, OpenShell, can be modified to work with other chips and hardware. And Nvidia is sharing reference designs for the whole software-and-hardware idea.
All of which makes OpenAI’s absence even more noticeable.
Clearly, OpenAI sees AI safety as an opportunity for independence from its major investor Nvidia, as well as a chance to show its own leadership. That is true even though it was OpenAI’s AI agents that scared the industry with the Hugging Face incident.
For instance, the company is developing its own safeguards for its research and products and is disclosing the worst incident it discovers.Meanwhile, OpenAI has its own AI cybersecurity consortium to for sharing information, called the Defense Factory. Those that signed on to support that idea include Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, and Google — many of the names that didn’t sign on to Nvidia’s technology-oriented approach.
And, truth be told, some level of fear is good for business. OpenAI is busy crafting cybersecurity into an enterprise offering, with everything from its own cyber-oriented model, Daybreak, to a growing network of partners that enterprises can hire to implement AI security.

articles.title: ¿Nuevos 'The Last of Us' en camino? Naughty Dog confirma dos proyectos en marcha
articles.text:
The Last of Us se mantiene como una de las sagas de videojuegos más celebradas por los fanáticos, que desde hace años le reclaman más a Naughty Dog. La adaptación televisiva de HBO ayudó a que los títulos de PlayStation llegaran a un público todavía más amplio, pero existe bastante impaciencia por saber si el estudio planea expandir la franquicia con nuevos juegos.
La buena noticia es que, por primera vez en mucho tiempo, Naughty Dog se ha pronunciado abiertamente sobre el futuro de The Last of Us. Fue el propio Neil Druckmann, jefe del estudio, quien informó a los fanáticos que tienen en marcha dos proyectos relacionados con la franquicia.
Todavía no se sabe de qué se tratan. De hecho, no está del todo claro si realmente se trata de nuevos juegos. Esto se debe a que Druckmann ha evitado usar la palabra "juegos" al referirse a estas nuevas iniciativas. El creativo se limitó a decir que se trata de nuevas "historias", aunque sí ha dejado algunas pistas que apuntan a que podrían ser propuestas gaming.
Según el líder del estudio, los nuevos proyectos van a "expandir el canon" de The Last of Us I y II. Pero también aclaró que todavía están en fases muy tempranas y que no pueden adelantar nada sobre qué tratan.
"Desde Grounded II, hemos hablado sobre la posibilidad de contar más historias en el mundo de The Last of Us. Tenemos un par de proyectos nuevos muy emocionantes en fases muy tempranas, por lo que no podemos decir mucho al respecto por ahora. Sí puedo adelantarles que ambos proyectos ampliarán el canon de The Last of Us más allá de la Parte I y la Parte II. El mundo de The Last of Us significa mucho para nosotros, y no volveríamos a él a menos que tuviéramos algo significativo que contar. Creemos que vale la pena contar estas historias", dijo Druckmann.
Nuevos proyectos de The Last of Us en camino, confirma Naughty Dog
La última parte de lo dicho de Neil Druckmann es la que genera más ilusión respecto de un futuro nuevo juego de The Last of Us. A mediados del año pasado, el creativo reconoció que la condición para regresar a la saga era tener una historia que le hiciera honor al legado de las entregas previas. La similitud entre ambos comentarios hace pensar que al menos uno de los dos proyectos puede ser un juego.
Tengamos en cuenta que en su momento hubo planes para un multijugador de The Last of Us que se canceló. De modo que no es la primera vez que se intenta expandir la saga en el ámbito jugable más allá de las dos entregas conocidas por todos.
Otro posible indicio de que las nuevas iniciativas pueden estar emparentadas con videojuegos es que Neil Druckmann ya no forma parte de la adaptación televisiva de The Last of Us. El jefe de Naughty Dog abandonó la serie a mediados del año pasado para enfocarse en proyectos de gaming.
Si realmente se está trabajando en nuevos juegos de The Last of Us, no te ilusiones con verlos en lo inmediato. La atención de los desarrolladores hoy está en Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. Dicho título se anunció hace un par de años y hasta aquí no se divulgaron muchos más detalles. De hecho, Druckmann reconoció que el primer vistazo en profundidad a la propuesta en cuestión se dará a conocer en 2027.

articles.title: AMD drops an EPYC $15,000, 256-core beast — EPYC 9006 Zen 6 'Venice' CPUs get full spec and pricing treatment, from $700 up to $14,904
articles.text:
AMD drops an EPYC $15,000, 256-core beast — EPYC 9006 Zen 6 'Venice' CPUs get full spec and pricing treatment, from $700 up to $14,904
After unveiling the EPYC 9006 (codenamed Venice) series in July and previewing a few impressive Zen 6 benchmarks, AMD has now released full pricing for its highly anticipated next-generation server chips. According to the list StorageReview obtained, AMD has big plans for the data center, with a wide range of SKUs from eight to 256 cores and pricing from $700 to $14,904.
As a quick refresher, AMD strategically divided the Venice lineup into two distinct segments. The SP7 platform is the flagship offering, delivering maximum memory capacity and throughput. It supports up to 16 memory channels, accommodating both RDIMMs and MDRDIMMs up to DDR5-12800. The platform offers up to 96 PCIe 6.0 lanes and supports Venice chips with TDPs between 400W and 600W.
The Venice parts designed for the SP7 socket offer scalable performance for enterprises. The lineup begins with the 64-core EPYC 9556, priced at $8,008, and extends to the flagship 256-core EPYC 9996, which commands $14,904. In retrospect, the EPYC 9996's price tag does not seem particularly shocking, especially since the previous-generation EPYC 9965 (codenamed Turin) launched at nearly the same price, around $14,800.
As is typical for server processors, the total price increases as the number of cores rises. However, the price per core actually decreases substantially as you move up the core ladder. The pricing dynamic is very notable with Venice. For example, the flagship EPYC 9996, with a massive 256 cores, comes out to just $58.21 per core, whereas the "entry-level" SP7 chip, the 64-core EPYC 9556, costs around $125.12 per core. As a result, higher core-count models are more attractive from a per-core value perspective for data centers, cloud service providers, and enterprises.

| EPYC 9556 | $8,008 | 64 / 128 | 2.75 / 4.30 | 384 | 1P / 2P | 300 | 
The SP7 SKUs support both 1P and 2P socket configurations. The latter, in particular, enables up to 512 Zen 6 cores in one system by pairing two EPYC 9996 chips on a single motherboard. That level of performance logically comes with a substantial investment, since the processors alone would cost $29,808 before factoring in the significant expense of memory today.
Among the nine SP7 SKUs, two models in particular stand out: the EPYC 9686F and EPYC 9586F. The "F" suffix means these chips feature maximum boost clock speeds, in this case, 5 GHz. While both are impressive in their own right, AMD optimized these parts to hit 5 GHz. Naturally, this level of optimization carries a price premium. For example, the 64-core EPYC 9586F costs almost as much as the 96-core EPYC 9656, despite offering 33% fewer cores. The trade-off is also apparent in the thermal envelope. The EPYC 9586F has a TDP that is 100W higher than the EPYC 9656.

The SP8 platform is a more streamlined and cost-effective counterpart to the SP7 platform for the Venice family. It supports eight-channel memory and does not embrace MRDIMMs. However, the limitation balances out by expansion possibilities, as the SP8 platform offers 128 PCIe 6.0 lanes, 33% more than the SP7 platform. Additionally, the SP8 platform has a lower thermal footprint, as these Zen 6 parts carry TDP ratings between 130W and 400W.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The SP8 platform offers an accessible entry point for organizations, with the octa-core EPYC 9106 priced at just $700. At the other end of the spectrum, the EPYC 9746, which is the top SP8 SKU, offers 128 Zen 6 cores at $11,679.
With the SP8 platform, we also see Zen 6 models with the “P” suffix, which indicates support for single-socket systems only. These variants deliver the same performance as their standard counterparts but at a significantly lower price. For example, the 128-core EPYC 9736P is 6% less expensive than the EPYC 9736. In an even more dramatic case, the 32-core EPYC 9356P retails for 26% less than the EPYC 9356.
One of the more unusual Venice chips is the 16-core EPYC 9176F. Despite its modest core count, it features a massive 192MB of L3 cache, 4X that of the 16-core EPYC 9116, while costing more than 3X as much. This translates to 12MB of L3 cache per core. With its high cache capacity and 5 GHz boost clock, AMD likely designed the EPYC 9176F for organizations seeking to minimize licensing costs for software priced per core.
AMD’s SP7 and SP8 platforms are scheduled to launch in the fourth quarter of this year and the first half of 2027, respectively. However, these Venice prices are not final, as AMD has stated that the list is subject to change. AMD will extend the lineup further later in 2027 with Venice-X chips, which use the company's 3D V-Cache stacking.

articles.title: Is your PC worth its weight in gold? This mini PC literally is — you'll need to be a multimillionaire to afford the solid-gold computer
articles.text:
Think the RAM crisis is pushing PC prices out of control? This $1.7m solid-gold mini PC will really make your wallet weep
Kubb Fanless goes gold
- Kubb has built a custom mini PC to order for a customer in Europe
- It's a Kubb Fanless made from 24-carat gold
- The value is reportedly $1.7 million, which isn't surprising given that the chassis is 13kg of solid gold
Think PCs are getting too pricey due to the RAM crisis? That's clearly true, but if you thought a top-end computer (with the likes of an RTX 5090 GPU) was getting ridiculously costly, it's nothing compared to this fanless rig which is fashioned from pure gold.
FanlessTech flagged up the PC from Kubb (via VideoCardz), a European manufacturer that specializes in fancy mini PCs. This take on the Kubb Fanless, a 120mm cube with no active cooling (fans), so it's silent, is made from 24-carat gold, rather than the aluminum that would normally be used for this model.
The gold version, which was built to order for a (presumably wealthy) customer, reportedly weighs 13kg (over six times the weight of the aluminum chassis), but the price tag is the real eye-opener here, as the PC runs to around $1.7 million (or £1.3 million / AU$2.4 million). Essentially the value of its weight in gold, of course.
As for the spec, the Kubb Fanless normally offers options of up to an Intel Core Ultra X7 358H or AMD Ryzen AI 5 340 CPU with up to 128GB of DDR5 RAM, although it's entirely possible that the buyer may have upped the spec with a custom request here.
Analysis: worth its weight in gold
What's interesting is that as FanlessTech points out, gold is a good material to make a fanless PC from due to its heat transference properties. Indeed, it offers around a 30% better level of thermal conductivity than aluminum, so you're actually getting much improved passive cooling here — for a price (and a half).
While this might appear to be an outlandish extravagance on the face of it, the other way to look at this solid-gold take on the Kubb Fanless is that it's an investment, in the same way as buying gold bars. The price of this precious metal has risen sharply since the pandemic, and I'm guessing the wealthy buyer has that in mind with this purchase — as well as showing off. (Don't take any of this as investment advice, I hasten to add — it certainly isn't offered as such.)

articles.title: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
articles.text:
The US executive branch is no longer acknowledging the existence of “artificial intelligence.” Going forward, official policy websites, policy documents, and press releases will refer only to “Super Intelligence,” thanks to a new executive order signed by President Donald Trump.
Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
“The word super is the best word of all,” Trump says.
“The word super is the best word of all, and it’s the simplest,” Trump said at an event announcing the launch of America.gov earlier on Tuesday, and said Chinese President Xi Jinping, who visited the White House last week, “loves it,” too. “We don’t want to hear artificial. Because it’s not artificial. It’s very powerful, it’s very brilliant. It’s going to mostly be put to good use and we’ll stop the bad use.” Artificial, he added, “is like the news. Fake news.” He first mentioned plans for the rebrand in a speech to the United Nations General Assembly last week, aiming to quell fears over AI advancing too quickly and posing a safety risk.
“It’s going to mostly be put to good use and we’ll stop the bad use”
Executive agencies won’t have to change past regulations or documents, but it could still constitute a real (and very strange) shift. Superintelligence is one of several industry terms for particularly powerful versions of artificial intelligence, but the Trump administration is seeking to use the term as a replacement for a broader statutory definition of AI. US officials will be expected not to even acknowledge the use of the terms “artificial intelligence” or “AI” in relevant settings.
Trump signed the executive order after a luncheon he hosted at the White House with tech CEOs and government officials to discuss what he’s now officially calling Super Intelligence. In brief public remarks after the meeting, flanked by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and surrounded by other attendees, Trump called the lunch “very productive,” and “extremely friendly.”
“There’s a belief that there should be tremendous self-regulation,” Trump said. “And we automatically have regulation with the Department of Justice, the FBI, all of that.” On the local level, where tech companies have faced the most hurdles in building out massive data centers needed to run their services, Trump says the firms will “work to make the community happy” by providing resources and economic support they may need. Ultimately, he says, “data centers are going to be very popular.”

articles.title: FBI tells ShinyHunters members to turn themselves in after recent arrest
articles.text:
The FBI is warning members of the ShinyHunters extortion group to turn themselves in after Dutch police arrested a man the bureau described as one of the group's alleged leaders.
"Today, our partners at the Dutch National Police announced the arrest of one of the alleged leaders of ShinyHunters, a group linked to cyberattacks in the United States, the Netherlands, and around the world," FBI Cyber Division Assistant Director Brett Leatherman said in a video released Tuesday.
Dutch police said the suspect is a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam who was arrested on September 15 and is suspected of playing a role within ShinyHunters and participating in a criminal organization.
"Following his arrest on September 15, a large amount of information was found on his laptop, including details about two murders that were to be committed abroad," the Dutch police announced today.
"There are indications that the suspect gave the order for this."
The Rotterdam District Court ruled Tuesday that the suspect will remain in pre-trial detention for at least another 90 days, while police said further arrests have not been ruled out.
The FBI says ShinyHunters and its alleged co-conspirators have breached more than 140 organizations since last year and collected at least $70 million in extortion payments.
ShinyHunters frequently targets corporate SSO accounts, third-party vendors, and cloud-based SaaS platforms, such as Salesforce and Snowflake, to steal sensitive data before extorting victims with threats to publish it.
The FBI's warning comes shortly after ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for a massive data breach at the bureau itself, which the threat actors told BleepingComputer that the breach involved exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day.
ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen between two and three terabytes of data from FBI systems, including information connected to multiple internal services.
The group later provided a sample of about 5,000 FBI personnel records to media organizations, including BleepingComputer, to support its claims.
While BleepingComputer declined the offer, 404 Media reported that the stolen information exposed names and personal data belonging to members of the FBI's Remote Operations Unit, a secretive team involved in hacking operations.
Reuters also reported that some of the exposed personnel were assigned to investigations involving China and Russia, raising concerns about the sensitivity of the information.
Despite the sensitivity of the stolen information, ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer that the FBI attack was never financially motivated, an extortion attempt, or intended to publish the data.
Instead, the threat actors claim it was done to dispute an FBI advisory that states ShinyHunters actors may exaggerate access to sensitive information, harass victims and their relatives, conduct swatting attacks, and falsely claim to possess compromising material.
The FBI is now taking a more public approach against the group, with Leatherman directly addressing the remaining ShinyHunters members in Tuesday's video.
"You've heard about the arrest of your colleague. We're confident you've seen or heard things in recent days that the public has not," Leatherman said.
"Other groups believed anonymity, or their friends, would protect them, and they were wrong. Arrests have a way of changing who is willing to talk, and seized infrastructure has a way of showing us who's left. "
Leatherman warned that investigators are continuing to gather information about those involved in the group and that they are actively being targeted.
"The longer you stay in this, the more we learn about you. You know how to find us, and we know how to find you. I suggest you reach out first while the choice is still yours."
Dutch police also clarified Tuesday that the arrested suspect was not detained as part of the investigation into the ShinyHunters breach of Dutch telecom provider Odido.

articles.title: SA’s Platybooks launches to help small businesses get paid in one step - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African startup Platybooks has launched an invoicing, quoting and light CRM platform that turns an accepted quote into an invoice with a built-in card payment link, settling funds directly into a small business’s own bank account.
Founded by Ché Overmeyer, Platybooks began life in 2023 as Invoiceer, before being shelved for around two years. Overmeyer revived the project in 2026, finished it and rebranded it as Platybooks.
A former photographer and tour operator, Overmeyer said the business admin was always the hardest part.
“In both of those the part I found hardest was keeping track of all my invoices and payments, spread across Excel spreadsheets, InvoiceTemplate.docx and the statements from the banking app,” he told Disrupt Africa. “I’m in my seventh professional year as a senior developer now, so I built the thing I kept wishing existed.”
With Platybooks, once a client accepts a quote, the invoice is created automatically. It is sent as a PDF carrying the fields required on a South African tax invoice, along with a card payment link. Payments go through Paystack into the business’s account, the invoice marks itself as paid, and automated reminders go out if it isn’t.
The platform also offers client management, a product catalogue, credit notes, recurring invoices, deposits, team roles and custom branding.
Overmeyer said the gap in the market is not a lack of invoicing software, but the fact that invoicing and payment remain separate.
“Xero, Zoho and QuickBooks all make you attach a gateway afterwards. Platybooks issues the invoice and the card payment link as one thing,” he said. “Xero and QuickBooks are good products. They’re just built for accountants, and priced and localised for somewhere else.”
Though Platybooks makes money through subscriptions, its four tiers are more locally-priced. The startup is bootstrapped, with the product currently being used by testers. Overmeyer said the company is now ready for a first funding round, aimed at distribution rather than product development.
“I have a complete product and no audience, and that’s the gap capital actually closes,” he said.
Platybooks is focused on South Africa for now, but Overmeyer sees a cheap route to expansion, as Paystack already operates in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and Uganda.
“South Africa proves the model; the second move is a repeat, not a pivot,” he said.

articles.title: Adani Family Office backs Nudge as startup pivots to rewards-led commerce
articles.text:
Adani Family Office backs Nudge as startup pivots to rewards-led commerce
Nudge, operated by iSocial Sports, is shifting from its earlier sports-led model towards receipt-based rewards, commerce and purchase intelligence for brands.
The Adani Family Office has backed Nudge, formerly known as BeBetta, in its shift towards rewards-led commerce and consumer intelligence.
The investor has backed the company across two consecutive rounds. Jhaveri Credits and Capital Limited, a listed Indian company with interests including securities and investments, has also backed the business, alongside other family offices, alternative investment funds and private investors from India and Dubai.
The company did not disclose the amount raised in its announcement.
The funding comes alongside a change in direction. BeBetta, which built a sports-led engagement and rewards business, has been rebranded as Nudge as it shifts towards rewards-led commerce and consumer intelligence.
The company claims it now has more than 3.3 million monthly active users, 400,000 daily active users, over 50,000 verified bills scanned each day, more than 200 brand partners and a presence across over 200 Indian cities.
Nudge allows consumers to scan purchase receipts from categories such as grocery, retail, dining and pharmacy to earn Nudge Coins, which can be redeemed with partner brands. On the enterprise side, it turns receipt information into structured, item-level data showing what consumers actually bought across online and offline channels. Such data can help brands move beyond measuring impressions or clicks towards tracking purchases.
“Receipts provide a direct and consented view of what people actually buy,” co-founder Meet Shah said, describing the company’s new focus as an effort to connect everyday purchases with rewards, commerce and actionable intelligence.
That proposition comes as Indian marketing becomes increasingly commerce-led. Advertising on e-retail platforms reached Rs 17,601 crore in 2025, up 55.9% year on year, according to the dentsu Digital Advertising Report 2026, with retail media accounting for 24.6% of digital media spending.
Meta and the Retailers Association of India have also highlighted the growing importance of omnichannel shopping, where consumers move between digital discovery and physical stores.
There is evidence of continued investor interest in adjacent consumer and rewards businesses. Consumer rewards platform Onpoint raised $600,000 in July from First Cheque and Whiteboard Capital, while women’s wellness brand Nua raised $50 million in September.
For Nudge, the next 12 to 24 months will centre on increasing the density of its purchase panel, launching paid brand-intelligence products and expanding its receipt-based model into MENA and Southeast Asia. The broader goal is a consumer-intelligence platform for the Global South, built from India.
Nudge said its consumer data is collected with explicit consent and used in aggregated and de-identified form.

articles.title: Microsoft Copilot confie parfois vos photos intimes à des êtres humains
articles.text:
Microsoft fait noter par des humains les retouches d’images produites par Copilot, dans le but d’entraîner son modèle. Des centaines de sous-traitants compareraient ainsi la photo envoyée par l’utilisateur et la version générée par l’IA. Les clichés leur parviennent tels quels, avec les visages, les proches et tout ce que l’on croyait réservé à la machine.
Des visages jamais floutés
Le dispositif porte sur l’outil d’édition d’images de Copilot, celui qui rajeunit un portrait, gomme un passant ou change un arrière-plan. Chaque relecteur reçoit la consigne tapée par l’utilisateur, l’image d’origine et la proposition de l’IA, puis note la fidélité de l’exécution. Ce travail relève de l’entraînement du modèle, un chantier distinct de la modération des contenus interdits, et le recrutement passe au moins en partie par Prolific, une plateforme de micro-travail en ligne.
Lire aussi : Microsoft dévoile son nouveau Copilot, une « super app » pour toutes ses IA
« Les visages ne sont jamais censurés, et beaucoup de requêtes sont de nature sexuelle, au consentement douteux », raconte l’un de ces relecteurs. Un autre dit être tombé sur un lot de « huit photos prises sous les jupes », qu’il a signalé à sa hiérarchie.
Interrogée, l’entreprise ne dément rien et renvoie à ses conditions d’utilisation : les données des clients servent « notamment à améliorer nos produits et à faire respecter notre code de conduite ». Aucun engagement de floutage ou d’anonymisation n’accompagne cette réponse, qui ne précise pas davantage si l’utilisateur peut s’opposer à cette relecture, ni combien de temps les images sont conservées. L’ampleur du dispositif se compterait au minimum en centaines de relecteurs, un chiffre que Microsoft ne confirme pas.
Sept ans après Siri, la même controverse
L’industrie a déjà trébuché sur ce terrain en juillet 2019, quand des sous-traitants d’Apple ont raconté écouter les enregistrements de Siri, conversations médicales et moments intimes compris. La firme avait suspendu son programme une semaine après les révélations. En France, l’affaire se prolonge devant la justice : après une plainte de la Ligue des droits de l’Homme en février 2025, le parquet de Paris a confié une enquête à l’Office anti-cybercriminalité, une procédure révélée en octobre de la même année.
Copilot ne fait pas cavalier seul dans ce recours aux petites mains. Deux semaines avant ces révélations, une enquête distincte décrivait des centaines de sous-traitants occupés à lire des conversations ChatGPT, pendant qu’Anthropic reconnaissait de son côté pratiquer aussi la relecture humaine. La retouche d’images ajoute un degré : au texte s’ajoutent désormais les visages.

articles.title: El ansiado AVE al País Vasco afronta su reto más descomunal: levantar siete viaductos en apenas siete kilómetros
articles.text:
A las localidades de Manzanos (Álava) y La Puebla de Arganzón (Burgos) las separan menos de seis kilómetros a recorrer en menos de 10 minutos por una apacible carretera. Pero cuando el objetivo es conectarlas con un tren que circula a más de 200 km/h, esa pequeña brecha se puede convertir en un acantilado.
Ese es el reto que tiene por delante Adif AV, encargada de supervisar uno de los mayores problemas de ingeniería al que se enfrenta la alta velocidad Burgos-Vitoria.
Un nuevo tramo. El Ministerio de Transportes ha confirmado la adjudicación para la construcción del tercer tramo de la línea de alta velocidad Burgos-Vitoria a través de Adif AV. Para sacar el tramo se invertirán 241,6 millones de euros pese a que sólo tiene una longitud de siete kilómetros.
Las vías se extenderán entre las localidades de Manzanos (Álava) y La Puebla de Arganzón (Burgos). O más bien podríamos decir casi que "sobrevolarán" porque el verdadero reto está en cómo llevar el tren de una a otra localidad.
Siete viaductos para siete kilómetros. Y es que en su anuncio, el Ministerio de Transportes destaca que el verdadero reto está en los siete viaductos que hay que construir para llevar el tren de uno a otro lado. Pese a que la extensión del tramo es de apenas siete kilómetros, serán necesarios siete pasos elevados para poder salvar todos los obstáculos que hay en el camino.
En total, el tren estará "sobrevolando" el suelo durante 2,5 kilómetros. Es decir, el 35% del tiempo que el tren circule por este punto lo hará sobre uno de estos viaductos. Teniendo en cuenta el tamaño de la infraestructura, veremos una concatenación de viaductos en muy poco espacio.
El más complicado. De todos ellos, uno destaca por encima del resto. Pese a que la suma total de viaductos medirá 2,5 kilómetros, sólo uno de ellos extenderá las vías por las alturas durante más de un kilómetro. Es el más complejo de los siete porque tiene numerosos obstáculos que salvar.
UN VISTAZO A...
Y es que esta infraestructura llevará las vías a 5o metros de altura y se sostendrá sobre un arco de hormigón de 222 metros. El objetivo es salvar de una sola vez el río Zadorra, la línea de ferrocarril convencional Madrid-Hendaya, la carretera nacional N-1 y la autovía A-1 que discurre paralela.
Un pasito más. Este tercer tramo adjudicado forma parte de los siete en los que se han dividido el tramo de alta velocidad Burgos-Vitoria para conectar esta línea con la Y vasca. De momento, de los siete tramos, Transportes destaca que ya hay cuatro en construcción, contratados o en licitación, sumando un total de 54,8 kilómetros.
De esos cuatro tramos en los que ya se trabaja, el primero en construcción, el Pancorbo-Ameyugo, también es muy complicado ya que el 77% de los 8,4 kilómetros discurren a lo largo de los tres túneles y tres viaductos que completan este paso. Además, se han hecho las primeras gestiones para la Variante Ferroviaria de Burgos y Valle de las Navas, de 16,7 kilómetros. En este caso se suceden otros seis viaductos más.
¿Para cuándo? Es lo que no está claro y es que no hay una fecha cerrada para la apertura del enlace de alta velocidad entre Burgos y Vitoria. El objetivo no está definido aunque José Antonio Santano, secretario de Estado del Ministerio de Transportes, apuntaba este mismo año a que espera que la línea esté lista "en cuatro o cinco años".
Y es que las dificultades técnicas son mayúsculas en este paso. Además de las obras ya mencionadas, el proyecto se ha retrasado en algunos puntos. Por ejemplo, en Piérnagas (Burgos) se firmó un contrato para ejecutar las obras en 34 meses. Sin embargo, en 2025 se tuvo que ampliar el plazo de ejecución en otros 15 meses dadas las dificultades y este mismo año se ha vuelto a ampliar el tiempo previsto en otros seis meses porque el terreno es demasiado inestable.
