articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 29, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 29, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, September 29, 2026.
From Ola Electric’s board approving Rs 1,000 Cr via a rights issue of partly paid-up shares to bolster its capital structure, to SiMa.ai, a physical AI startup that has raised $150 million in a Series C round, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
As AI makes copying easier, this product leader says trust is the real edge
A young composer built a backyard studio in 1989 and did everything himself: composing, producing, engineering. By 1992, his first film soundtrack was a nationwide hit. Decades on, he is still refining what film music sounds like. That composer was A.R. Rahman.
Kunal Shrestha, VP of Product at Responsive, opened his session at DevSparks Chennai 2026 with this story, using it as a frame for developers watching AI make software cheaper and faster to build, and by extension, easier to replicate. His session, titled ‘The new moat for developers: moving beyond the feature’, set out to answer where differentiation goes once features stop being defensible on their own.
Latest News
Ola Electric plans Rs 1,000 Cr rights issue, appoints new compliance officer
Ola Electric is taking steps to strengthen its finances and leadership as competition intensifies in India’s electric two-wheeler market.
In a board meeting on September 28, 2026, the Bengaluru-based company approved plans to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue of partly paid-up equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each, according to a BSE investor filing.
Alongside the fundraising plan, the board appointed Deepa Bansal as the new Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Bansal has over 11 years of experience in secretarial and governance roles, and has previously worked at Medi Assist Healthcare, Tessolve Semiconductor, and Kothari Petrochemicals. She will take charge of the key managerial role with immediate effect.
Funding News
WEH Ventures marks first close of Rs 250 Cr Fund III
WEH Ventures, a seed-stage venture capital firm, has announced the first close of Fund III with a target corpus Rs 250 crore. Though it did not disclose the quantum of funds raised in the first close.
A statement from WEH Ventures said the first close has attracted participation from a mix of family offices, exited founders and senior corporate and technology executives. Early backers include Play Capital, a Nordic Fund of Fund (FoF); family offices such as Eraya, Twin & Bull Investments and Heritage Investments; exited founders from companies including Oziva and GS Labs; senior executives and CEOs from companies such as Thermax, Haleon, Lenovo and PNB MetLife; as well as senior Silicon Valley executives associated with companies including Arlo and Intuitive Surgical.
Physical AI startup SiMa.ai raises $150M in Series C
SiMa.ai, a physical AI startup founded by Krishna Rangasayee, has raised $150 million in a Series C round co-led by Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify, with participation from Alter Venture Partners and Dell Technologies Capital.
The round also saw participation from StepStone Group, AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital, and J.P. Morgan. The funding values SiMa.ai at $1.45 billion and takes its total funding raised to $500 million.
The company said the fresh capital will be used to scale its agentic software platform for physical AI, Palette Neat, and develop hardware products, such as machine learning IP, chiplets, and system-on-chips (SoCs).
Arma Capital invests Rs 10 cr in EBG Group
Maharashtra-based Arma Capital has invested Rs 10 crore across EBG Group’s wellness, food and family businesses, marking its entry into the Hyderabad-headquartered group’s consumer-facing brands. The investment covers Carlton Wellness Centres in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chandigarh, along with franchise partnerships for NATUF Café, Adhira & Appa Café and Chhota Bheem Family Café in Hyderabad.
The investment is the first phase of a larger partnership under which Arma Capital plans to invest more than Rs 100 crore over the next five years. The funding will support the expansion of Carlton Wellness Center, Tarzan Nature Retreat, Adhira and Appa Coffee, Natuf Cafe, Chhota Bheem Café and upcoming EBG brands across Chandigarh, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi NCR.
Healthtech startup Primerry secures Rs 7.1 Cr in pre-seed round
Pediatric healthcare brand Primerry has raised Rs 7.1 crore in pre-seed funding from investors such as Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, and various angel investors. Co-founded by Rushabh Nandu and Dr. Nihar Parekh, Primerry focuses on children aged 2 to 14, offering modern, clinically credible, and easy-to-use healthcare products.
The company will use the capital to expand its founding team, boost R&D, and roll out eight initial products priced between Rs 499 and Rs 1,499. Primerry plans to distribute through its D2C platform, quick-commerce channels, pharmacies, and specialty stores, alongside launching PocDoc—a customisable carrying case designed to make healthcare engaging for kids.
Other News
IBM and Yotta announce agentic AI platform for Indian organisations
IBM and Yotta Data Services have launched the Sovereign Agentic AI Platform for Indian organisations, enabling them to scale AI agents locally while keeping data, operations, and governance strictly within India.
Powered by IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Yotta’s Shakti Cloud, the solution integrates enterprise agentic control with sovereign compute, GPU infrastructure, and model development tools via Shakti Studio. Available through Yotta’s Panvel and Greater Noida regions, the platform supports workflows like security operations, HR automation, and document processing. Leadership from both companies emphasized that this collaboration provides an end-to-end, compliant AI stack to help enterprises safely transition from AI experimentation to full production.
Flipkart announces expansion of Ekart’s supply chain ahead of The Big Billion Days
Flipkart’s logistics arm, Ekart, expanded its supply chain for the upcoming festive season by adding 14 million cubic feet of warehouse space and 900 delivery hubs. To accelerate deliveries across over 8,200 facilities and 1,200 microfulfillment centers, Ekart added 750 new PIN codes, including remote regions like Leh, Kargil, and the Northeast.
To empower MSMEs, 2.5 crore seller products were pre-positioned in fulfillment centers. Flipkart created over 2.5 lakh seasonal jobs, providing delivery partners with AI-powered quick onboarding, bonuses, and comprehensive medical coverage. Supply chain head Hemant Badri noted that these upgrades ensure faster deliveries nationwide.
DeepTek partners with unitaid and CHAI to expand affordable AI TB screening in LMICs
DeepTek has introduced its Global Access Pricing initiative through a collaboration with Unitaid and the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) to expand tuberculosis (TB) screening across 138 low- and middle-income countries.
The model reduces the cost of DeepTek’s WHO-recommended Chest X-ray AI solution to roughly one-third of its previous price, allowing health systems to screen up to three times more people within existing budgets. The all-inclusive annual subscription covers installation, training, and maintenance for online, offline, and mobile settings. Beyond TB, the AI tool detects over 20 chest abnormalities, helping bridge critical radiologist shortages in high-burden regions.
Melento and Gnani AI to deliver voice-enabled Agentic AI for enterprises
Melento (formerly SignDesk) has partnered with Gnani AI to integrate frontier Voice AI with agentic AI orchestration, transitioning enterprise voice workflows from scripted responses to actionable execution.
By pairing Gnani AI's multi-language voice models—processing over 30 million daily interactions—with Melento’s enterprise platform, the collaboration enables AI agents to understand intent, make decisions, and execute tasks directly within business systems. Designed for regulated sectors like BFSI, insurance, and pharma, the solution automates complex customer and employee workflows—including voice-led onboarding, KYC, real-time contract updates, and internal approvals—while ensuring compliance, security, and seamless deployment.
Flipkart partners Casio to expand nationwide after-sales support
Flipkart’s after-sales arm, F1 Info Services, has partnered with Casio to deliver walk-in service support across India. The collaboration provides repair and replacement services for Casio calculators across 250+ centers in 23 states, alongside repair services for watches and electronic musical instruments in select cities.
Covering both in-warranty and out-of-warranty products, the initiative leverages F1’s company-owned, company-operated (COCO) model and technicians trained directly by Casio. This strategic partnership strengthens Casio’s post-purchase footprint while expanding F1 Info Services’ reach in delivering reliable, professionally managed after-sales support nationwide
Target expands Bengaluru campus with 830,000 sq ft office
Target in India has expanded its Bengaluru campus with a new 830,000 sq ft office at Embassy Manyata Business Park. Located across the road from Target’s existing facility, the new building creates an integrated campus aimed at improving collaboration among the company’s more than 5,700 employees.
The 10-floor office includes 22 collaboration spaces, 25 meeting rooms on every floor, a 1,200-seater cafeteria, gym, recreation and play zone, dance and yoga studio, and seven wellness rooms. The workplace also incorporates elements of India’s art and craft heritage alongside Target’s brand identity. Target has operated in India for more than 21 years, with teams working across technology-enabled retail functions including merchandising, supply chain, fulfilment, cybersecurity, digital and marketing.
Omnivore-backed agrifood startups reach 20.81 million farmers
Agrifood startups backed by venture capital firm Omnivore have reached 20.81 million smallholder farmers and 61,711 rural MSMEs across India, according to the firm’s 2026 Impact Reports covering two funds. The reports track outcomes across businesses operating in farmer services, rural finance, consumer brands and deeptech. Omnivore’s portfolio includes DeHaat, Arya.ag, Sid’s Farm, Varaha, Farmley and Pixxel. Across the two funds, portfolio companies have generated $5.64 billion in combined economic value for smallholder farmers directly and indirectly, while 11.55 million hectares have been brought under sustainable agriculture. The reports also recorded $2.18 billion in insurance coverage for rural households and $63.62 million in loans to rural MSMEs. Omnivore has invested in India’s agriculture and food economy since 2011 and currently manages $295 million across two active venture funds.
HCLTech study highlights AI transformation gap in wealth management
HCLTech’s latest research has found that 84% of global wealth management firms believe their operating models require fundamental redesign to realise the potential of artificial intelligence. The study, based on 1,066 AI personas representing senior wealth management decision-makers across 17 global markets, found that 98% of leadership teams are actively pursuing an AI agenda, while slightly more than 7% are building agentic AI capabilities.
The research identifies three blind spots: firms continue funding AI primarily for efficiency, underinvest in proprietary client data and insights, and often fail to measure AI’s impact on growth, revenue and clients. HCLTech said first-party and behavioural data were ranked as more valuable differentiators than technology infrastructure, cloud platforms or AI partnerships.
DraperU India Demo Day sees Rs 25 lakh commitments for two startups
DraperU India’s latest Founders Program concluded with a Demo Day in Hyderabad, where 13 startups pitched to more than 150 investors, venture capitalists, ecosystem leaders and industry experts. Ordo and WearSynapse secured investment commitments of Rs 25 lakh each from DraperU India, along with an investment commitment from Hyderabad Angels. Both startups also earned opportunities to represent DraperU India at Draper University’s Hero Training Program in Silicon Valley. Ordo, WearSynapse and Creator Studio additionally won a share of IDFC FIRST Bank’s ₹90,000 prize pool.
The Demo Day followed a 12-day residential programme focused on product development, business models, go-to-market strategies, storytelling and fundraising. Participating startups represented sectors including deeptech, physical AI, healthtech, AI-native SaaS, cybersecurity, defence tech and proptech.
Pine Labs extends technology partnership with Woolworths
Pine Labs has extended its technology partnership with Woolworths Group to strengthen the retailer’s gift card ecosystem through enhanced platform capabilities, deeper API integrations and support for new digital stored-value experiences. Through its Qwikcilver subsidiary, Pine Labs powers the technology platform supporting Woolworths’ gift card programmes. The expanded partnership will focus on modernising gift card infrastructure across physical and digital channels, while improving scalability and integration with broader commerce ecosystems. Qwikcilver’s platform supports gift card issuance, processing, transaction management and omnichannel programmes. Pine Labs said its API-led, modular architecture allows enterprises to progressively add new use cases using existing infrastructure. The partnership comes as retailers increasingly integrate gifting, customer engagement and digital commerce, making stored-value platforms an important component of enterprise commerce infrastructure.
KL University, Salesforce to establish Tableau Lab
KL University has partnered with Salesforce to establish a Tableau Lab aimed at strengthening data literacy, analytical thinking and AI skills among students. The initiative will provide hands-on exposure to Tableau and introduce students to agentic analytics and real-world business applications.
The programme will cover foundational data skills through advanced AI-powered analytics, with students working on industry datasets and business case simulations. Learners will gain experience in dashboard creation, conversational analytics, predictive insights and data storytelling, with exposure to Tableau Agent and Tableau Pulse. The initiative will be available to undergraduate, postgraduate and research students and include business projects, analytics hackathons and e-learning modules. Salesforce will also support faculty through a Train-the-Trainer programme. Eligible students and faculty will receive joint course-completion certificates, while graduates may access industry interactions through Salesforce’s Campus to Career Connect initiative.
CtrlS, Ciena to build five metro networks for AI and cloud demand
CtrlS Datacenters is partnering with Ciena to build five metro networks connecting nine data centres across Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, New Delhi and Noida. The networks are designed to deliver up to 100 Tb/s of capacity and support rising bandwidth requirements driven by artificial intelligence and cloud services. The initiative forms part of a larger Managed Optical Fiber Network deployment for a leading hyperscaler and is aimed at strengthening high-speed connectivity for India’s growing digital infrastructure requirements. CtrlS is deploying Ciena’s WaveLogic 5 Extreme-powered Waveserver platform and 6500 Reconfigurable Line System, supported by Ciena’s services team. Ciena’s Navigator Network Control Suite will help automate network operations and accelerate service delivery. CtrlS currently operates 19 data centres across nine Indian markets, with more than 370 MW of capacity.
Olyv appoints Amod Kumar Choudhary as VP-Business
Digital lending platform Olyv has appointed Amod Kumar Choudhary as Vice President–Business, where he will lead business and growth initiatives. Choudhary joins Olyv from OneCard, where he served as Chief Marketing Officer and handled business P&L, customer acquisition, portfolio spend, revenue, product development and consumer experience. At Olyv, he will oversee commercial functions spanning growth and marketing, business strategy, customer engagement and portfolio development. He brings more than two decades of experience across fintech, consumer businesses, retail, sales, marketing and P&L management.
Kapture CX appoints Kruti Khandelwal as VP-Marketing
Agentic AI platform Kapture CX has appointed Kruti Khandelwal as Vice President–Marketing as the company prepares for its next phase of growth in India and international markets. Khandelwal will oversee the company’s marketing charter covering brand, content, product marketing, public relations, partner marketing, events and demand generation. Kapture CX serves more than 1,000 enterprise customers across 18 countries and has achieved profitability with a business built primarily around India.

articles.title: Google commence doucement à enterrer ses Chromebooks
articles.text:
Si vous achetez un Chromebook aujourd'hui, ses mises à jour s'arrêteront en 2034, soit huit ans plus tard, alors que Google promet dix ans de support. L'information figure dans une page d'assistance publiée par Google.
Fin des mises à jour en 2034, migration vers Googlebook OS à préciser
Pour son cycle de support Google s'engage à mettre à jour ses Chromebook pendant dix ans. Un modèle acheté en 2026 devrait donc être suivi jusqu'en 2036. Or, la page de Google annonce la fin des mises à jour à 2034. Pour les appareils éligibles dont le cycle dépasse cette date, Google s'engage à accompagner le passage vers Googlebook OS, sans pour autant dire quand ni comment.
Pour mémoire, Googlebook OS est le système des nouveaux ordinateurs portables de Google. Il repose sur la pile technologique d'Android, à laquelle Google ajoute l'interface de bureau de ChromeOS. Un peu plus tôt ce mois-ci, nous rapportions que Google promettait jusqu'à 10 ans de mises à jour pour les Googlebook, tout en gardant les Chromebook au catalogue, notamment sur l'entrée et le milieu de gamme.
Reste la migration. Google affirme que de nombreux Chromebook professionnels récents pourront passer sous Googlebook OS, mais la liste des modèles concernés et la marche à suivre viendront plus tard. L'entreprise assure aussi que les Chromebook actuels restent pris en charge selon sa politique de mises à jour. Les licences ChromeOS Enterprise Upgrade et Education Upgrade, qui donnent accès aux outils de gestion du parc, gardent leurs fonctions sur ces machines. Par contre, elles ne pourront pas être transférées et pour gérer un appareil passé sous Googlebook OS, il faudra acquérir une nouvelle licence.
Bon, en pratique, ces deux années de support en moins ne sont pas comparables à des machines équipées de Windows et il est peu probable que beaucoup de Chromebook actuels soient encore en service en 2034. Pour Google, il s'agit sans doute d'une façon de décourager les écoles et les entreprises de garder ces ordinateurs. Côté calendrier, les premiers Googlebook, pensés pour le grand public, arrivent en France le 5 octobre. Reste qu'aucun des cinq constructeurs partenaires n'a conçu son premier modèle pour les écoles ni pour les organisations qui équipent de grands parcs, et les premiers outils de gestion arriveront à partir du second semestre 2027.

articles.title: Oracle expands AI agent features with Fusion Claw - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Oracle expands AI agent features with Fusion Claw
Oracle Corp. today is introducing an agentic software runtime that lets its Fusion applications carry out complex business tasks, from reconciling accounting entries to revising staffing plans when conditions change.
Fusion Claw combines large language models for reasoning and planning with conventional software for calculations and transaction processing. Oracle is also announcing 25 applications powered by Claw, bringing its portfolio of Fusion Agentic Applications to 75.
Fusion Claw takes Oracle agents beyond the simpler tasks addressed by its earlier agentic applications. Those could pursue focused goals such as improving renewals, said Natalia Rachelson, Oracle’s senior vice president of Fusion Applications and product management. In contrast, Claw is intended for longer-running work that requires extensive modeling, optimization and repeated changes to a plan.
“We did not previously have solutions for advanced optimization,” Rachelson said.
In a staffing example, a Fusion Claw agent might consider employee qualifications, availability, labor rules and cost targets, then propose scheduling options. It would evaluate the options, perform the necessary calculations and, if authorized, make changes in the system of record. It could also autonomously reopen the plan if an employee called in sick.
Oracle said the Fusion Claw architecture limits the use of expensive AI models. Claw uses a model when it needs to reason about a problem, while transactions and calculations over large datasets take place outside the model. The initial release supports frontier models from Google LLC’s Gemini and OpenAI Group PBC. Rachelson said Oracle plans to support more models but did not provide specifics. Users currently can’t select their own open lower-tier models for Claw tasks.
The 25 agentic applications include tools for investigating accounting exceptions, developing workforce staffing plans, consolidating shipments and planning sales territories. Oracle said Claw can also work with third-party systems through application programming interfaces, Model Control Protocol and the Agent2Agent protocol.
Giving software authority to change business records raises questions about oversight. Oracle said customers can set objectives, permissions, risk thresholds and approval requirements within what it calls an Enterprise Operating Envelope. They can choose a mode in which an employee reviews a plan or allows the application to execute within delegated authority. Claw runs in an isolated environment that prevents the language model from directly updating Fusion business objects, Rachelson said.
Once a task completes, an “Outcome Receipt” is generated showing the policies applied, decisions made and transactions performed. Rachelson said the receipt contains more context than a conventional audit log, including the full text of policies used during the task.
Oracle ultimately expects customers to authorize more work without individual approvals as they become comfortable with Fusion Claw.
“Honestly, any task can be in full auto mode,” Rachelson said, though she expects organizations to start with more human review and expand automation as they gain experience. The company did not provide measured cost savings or evidence of how the applications perform in production.
Oracle said all 25 Claw-powered agentic applications are available now. Claw is included at no additional charge with the company’s agentic applications product, which requires a separate purchase from a standard Fusion subscription. Customers pay for AI units consumed as work is completed.

articles.title: Vibe Coding für Produktteams: Vom App-Prototyp zur getesteten Produktentscheidung
articles.text:
Vibe Coding für Produktteams: Vom App-Prototyp zur getesteten Produktentscheidung
Vibe Coding verändert gerade, wie Produktteams über Software entscheiden, die es noch nicht gibt. Statt eine Idee zu beschreiben, in Meetings dafür zu werben und auf freie Kapazität bei Design oder Entwicklung zu warten, bauen Produktmanager:innen heute selbst einen klickbaren App-Prototyp, ohne dafür eine Zeile Code von Hand zu schreiben. Bis vor Kurzem blieb jede Diskussion darüber vor allem eines: eine Frage der Meinungsstärke, weil niemand etwas zum Anfassen hatte.
Der Wechsel betrifft weniger das Werkzeug als die Reihenfolge. Erst prüfst du, welche Annahme hinter einer Idee wirklich riskant ist, dann entsteht dazu ein Prototyp. Erst wenn das Feedback stimmt, beginnt die eigentliche Entwicklung.
Was Vibe Coding in der Produktarbeit leistet
Der Begriff Vibe Coding bezeichnet die Arbeitsweise, Code direkt aus einer Beschreibung in natürlicher Sprache von einem KI-Agenten schreiben zu lassen. Der Unterschied zum klassischen Mockup ist trotzdem funktional. Statt einer Skizze in Figma entsteht ein Entwurf, den du tatsächlich bedienen kannst, mit echten Formularen und Klickpfaden. Wer sein KI-Werkzeug mit dem eigenen Code oder mit Screenshots der Anwendung füttert, bekommt ein Ergebnis, das aussieht wie das echte Produkt statt wie eine generische Vorlage. Entscheider:innen sehen dann etwas Konkretes statt einer weiteren Folie, und Testpersonen reagieren auf eine reale Oberfläche statt auf eine Beschreibung.
Übertragen auf den Arbeitsalltag heißt das: Statt Interviews und andere Kundendaten von Hand zu einem Meinungsbild zusammenzutragen, fütterst du ein KI-Werkzeug mit genau diesen Quellen und befragst es nach wiederkehrenden Mustern. So zeigt sich, welches Kundenbedürfnis eine anstehende Entscheidung tatsächlich betrifft, und welches nur am lautesten war.
Zur ehrlichen Einordnung gehört, dass ein Prototyp ein Prototyp bleibt. Er ersetzt keine geprüfte Architektur und keine Sicherheitsprüfung für den produktiven Betrieb. Und ein Klick-Dummy, der bereits fertig wirkt, verleitet Testpersonen erfahrungsgemäß dazu, den Feinschliff zu bewerten statt der Idee dahinter. Ein altbekanntes Risiko beim Testen früher Entwürfe, das mit KI-generierten Oberflächen eher zu- als abnimmt.
Onlinekurs „Vibe Coding für Produktteams: vom Kundenfeedback zur getesteten Idee“
Wie sich das in der Praxis anfühlt, zeigt der Onlinekurs „Vibe Coding für Produktteams: Vom Kundenfeedback zur getesteten Idee“ von t3n PRO am 14. Oktober 2026. Anhand eines durchgehenden Fallbeispiels aus der Produktpraxis verfolgst du den Weg von einer offenen Produktfrage bis zu einer Entscheidung, die das Entwicklungsteam ohne Rückfragen übernehmen kann: Kundenstimmen ordnen und Prototypen im Look des eigenen Produkts bauen.
Hendrik Hemken, AI-Consultant und Gründer der Beratung Beyond7, leitet den Kurs. Bevor er heute Unternehmen dabei begleitet, agentische KI-Workflows einzuführen, hat er selbst über zwölf Jahre Produktteams im FinTech-Umfeld geführt. Diese Doppelperspektive prägt seinen Blick auf Vibe Coding: Sein Ausgangspunkt ist die Entscheidung, die am Ende ansteht. Das Werkzeug kommt danach.
Product Manager und Product Owner, deren Entscheidungen bislang eher aus Meinungsrunden als aus Tests entstehen, profitieren hier am meisten. Genauso profitieren Gründer:innen, die eine Hypothese prüfen wollen, bevor Budget in die Umsetzung fließt. Programmier-Vorwissen brauchst du dafür nicht, erste Erfahrung mit einem KI-Chat wie Claude oder ChatGPT reicht.
Wer live nicht dabei sein kann, bekommt die Aufzeichnung sowie die Slides des Dozenten im Anschluss an den Kurs.
Der Kurs „Vibe Coding für Produktteams: Vom Kundenfeedback zur getesteten Idee“ findet am 14. Oktober 2026 von 10:00-12:00 Uhr statt und kostet 149 €. t3n-PRO-Member nehmen wie immer kostenlos teil. Hier geht’s zum Shop!

articles.title: AI Data Centers Make Power, Cooling Critical to Scaling - EE Times
articles.text:
AI is reshaping the role of data centers, turning them from largely invisible cloud infrastructure into strategic assets where power delivery, cooling, advanced packaging, and semiconductors have become as critical as compute performance.
Speaking at EE Power Asia 2026, Ang Wee Seng, executive director of the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association (SSIA), said AI has shifted the industry’s focus beyond processor performance toward the physical infrastructure required to deploy and scale AI systems.
“AI has transformed computing from a digital challenge into a physical infrastructure race,” he said. “AI is not only about software revolution anymore. It is an infrastructure revolution.”
According to Ang, traditional measures of computing progress such as processor speed and transistor density remain important, but AI deployment increasingly depends on factors including available power, rack density, cooling capacity, memory bandwidth, and deployment speed. Large AI data centers can already draw more than 100 MW of power, while worldwide data center spending is expected to exceed $650 billion this year.
The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is being driven by four major trends: the transition from model training to continuous inference, growing memory and bandwidth requirements, increasing investment in sovereign AI infrastructure, and ongoing cloud modernization centered on accelerated computing.
These shifts are creating new engineering constraints. “The next bottleneck may not be, can we design the next chip? It may be, can we power it? Can we connect it? Can we cool it down? Can we deploy it fast enough?” Ang said.
Infrastructure becomes the limiting factor
Ang noted that site selection for hyperscale AI facilities is increasingly determined by access to power rather than land availability. Grid connectivity, substations, cooling infrastructure, renewable energy availability, and fiber connectivity have become key considerations.
“In many cases, facility follows where the power is, not the other way around,” he said.
Energy efficiency has also become a central design objective. Every watt consumed ultimately generates heat, increasing cooling requirements and adding further power demand. Improvements in power conversion efficiency therefore translate directly into greater usable compute capacity.
“The power chain is no longer peripheral” Ang said. “It is part of the AI scaling roadmap now.”
At the system level, AI is also changing data center architecture. Rather than treating servers as independent units, AI deployments increasingly organize accelerators, networking, power delivery, and cooling around tightly integrated rack-scale systems.
“The rack is becoming the new unit of design,” Ang said. “The system is the product. The rack is the platform. The power architecture is the competitive differentiator.”
Semiconductor ecosystem expands beyond processors
While GPUs have become the focal point of AI computing, Ang said future AI platforms will rely on heterogeneous computing architectures combining CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, custom accelerators and high-speed interconnects.
Advanced packaging, chiplets, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), silicon photonics, and optical networking have consequently become integral to AI system design.
“Memory bandwidth is now central to AI scaling,” he said, noting that HBM shortages and advanced packaging capacity have become strategic constraints across the semiconductor supply chain.
He added that optimizing AI infrastructure now requires balancing silicon, packaging, boards, cooling systems, networking, and power delivery rather than maximizing the performance of individual components.
Power electronics move to center stage
Ang argued that power semiconductors are moving from supporting technologies to strategic enablers of AI infrastructure.
Power enters AI facilities through multiple conversion stages—from utility grids and UPS systems to rack-level power shelves and voltage regulators—where even small efficiency gains can significantly reduce heat generation and operating costs at hyperscale.
He highlighted complementary roles for silicon, silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN), emphasizing that each technology addresses different parts of the power architecture.
“The question is not simply which material should win,” Ang said. “The better question to ask is, where does each technology create the greatest system level value?”
Looking ahead, Ang said future AI infrastructure should be evaluated using broader system metrics such as tokens per joule, watts per square meter, conversion efficiency, and deployment speed rather than compute performance alone.
“The future data centers will not be won by the fastest chip alone,” he said. “It will be won by the most efficient integrated system.”
He concluded that the semiconductor industry’s next opportunity extends across the full AI infrastructure stack, from power devices and packaging to materials, testing, and system integration.
“For years now, the semiconductor industry has powered the digital economy,” Ang said. “Now we are being asked to power the AI economy.”
—This article was originally published in the EE Times Recommend ASEAN e-guide July 2026.

articles.title: How Zimbabweans are getting into Africa’s biggest IPO
articles.text:
A Zimbabwean investor can buy into Africa’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), but the journey starts with paperwork, approvals and a bank transfer, not an app.
Bard Santner Investors (BSI), a Zimbabwean asset management firm, is facilitating the country’s participation in Dangote Refinery’s $1.6 billion IPO, giving local investors access to a share sale that opened to investors across Africa on September 14. But the process also reveals how much of cross-border investing remains manual even as fintech platforms make domestic investing increasingly digital.
The Dangote IPO is testing Africa’s investment infrastructure from two directions: Nigerian investment apps struggled with a surge in retail demand, while Zimbabwean investors are relying on Bard Santner to navigate foreign-exchange controls, custody and cross-border settlement.
“So far, because of the time, we couldn’t do online applications. We are doing it more manually,” Ngoni Chikowore, head of asset management at Bard Santner, told TechCabal in an interview on Tuesday.
That manual process does not mean Zimbabweans are sitting out one of Africa’s biggest investment opportunities. Instead, BSI has built a route for investors to participate in the Nigerian offer.
“Because we are all outside Nigeria, the application is treated as an offshore or foreign investment in Nigeria,” Chikowore said. In Zimbabwe, the investment is also treated as an offshore transaction, requiring exchange-control approval.
BSI, which is regulated as an asset manager in Zimbabwe, obtains the required approvals before moving clients’ funds through Ecobank Zimbabwe, the country’s digital banking pioneer, to Ecobank Nigeria. On the Nigerian side, Ecobank’s nominee structure holds the assets and submits the IPO application on BSI’s behalf.
“When we then do a subscription from this side, they will then upload a completed form on behalf of us and submit it for the IPO,” Chikowore said.
He said the $20,000 threshold is intended to meet the minimum requirement for eligible African investors participating through BSI, while leaving room for adjustments to the final share allocation.
Dangote has marketed the IPO as a broad retail opportunity, with the offer comprising 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 (40c) each and targeting about $1.6 billion. The minimum Nigerian subscription is 10 shares, or ₦5,250 ($3.96), allowing much smaller domestic investors to participate.
For Zimbabweans, however, the BSI route provides a way into the same deal despite the additional regulatory and settlement requirements. The prospectus says the offer closes on October 13, with listing expected in November, giving BSI a narrow window to complete approvals, funding and applications for participating Zimbabwean clients within the deadline.
That infrastructure was tested from another direction when Nigerian digital investment platforms came under pressure after the IPO opened. On September 14, TechCabal reported outages at Bamboo and Cowrywise.
Although BSI is Zimbabwean, the disruption in Nigeria threatened to disrupt IPO applications and payments from Zimbabwean and other African investors. Chikowore said the outage did not ultimately derail the process because client funds move through the banking system, while BSI retains records confirming investors’ participation.
“The only risk is if maybe before allotment,” he stated. “When we transfer the funds, we are transferring them through the banking sector through Ecobank Zimbabwe to Ecobank Nigeria, so we have evidence or a claim to say we have participated.”
The investment material links the Dangote opportunity to businesses spanning mining, cement and fertiliser manufacturing, power generation and fuel transportation, including a 2,000-kilometre petroleum pipeline running from Namibia’s Walvis Bay through Botswana to Bulawayo.
“What we are working towards is automating our process,” he said. The goal is eventually to let clients access their investment accounts through internet banking.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: iPhone Duo : Apple préparerait 5 nouveaux modes veille pour son smartphone pliant
articles.text:
Si nous avons déjà pu avoir un bel aperçu de l’iPhone Duo lors de la dernière keynote, Apple semble encore réserver quelques surprises pour sa commercialisation prévue pour le 23 octobre prochain. En effet, le leaker Pdfu a effectué une analyse approfondie du code d’iOS 27.1 et il y a découvert 5 modes En veille (StandBy) pour l’iPhone Duo qui n’ont pas encore été annoncés par Apple. Au programme : deux modes consacrés à la maison connectée, deux modes présentant des effets visuels et un mode entièrement dédié à Snoopy.
Cinq nouveaux modes « En veille » pour l’iPhone Duo
Pour rappel, Apple a pour l’instant annoncé 7 modes En veille (StandBy) pour l’iPhone Duo : Horloge analogique, Horloge numérique, Calendrier classique, Météo, Photos, Albums partagés et Modulaire. Tous ces modes seront personnalisables avec différentes couleurs et polices.
Le leaker Pdfu a quant à lui découvert cinq autres modes En veille qui n’ont pour l’instant jamais été évoqués par Apple, à savoir : Home Camera, Home Modular, Flow, Fade et Snoopy. Les modes Home Camera et Home Modular sont consacrés à la maison connectée. Le premier devrait permettre de visualiser le flux d’une seule caméra ou une grille de neuf caméras maximum, tandis que le second, Home Modular, est consacré aux commandes de la maison connectée.
Le mode Flow devrait offrir un affichage interactif et animé, tandis que le mode Fade pourrait proposer un effet visuel où les éléments apparaissent ou disparaissent progressivement. Enfin, comme son nom l’indique, le mode Snoopy serait entièrement consacré au célèbre chien. Les modes Home Camera, Home Modular et Flow devraient proposer des options de personnalisation (choix de la couleur, de la police, du style, etc.), similaires à celles des cadrans de watchOS. Au total, l’iPhone Duo devrait donc proposer 13 modes En veille (StandBy) lors de son lancement. Il faut dire que la possibilité de transformer le premier iPhone pliant d’Apple en réveil de chevet avait fait forte impression lors de la keynote de rentrée d’Apple.
Quid de l’Apple Pencil ?
En parlant des surprises que pourrait encore nous réserver l’iPhone Duo, il reste un point à éclaircir, celui de l’Apple Pencil. Selon Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, l’entreprise à la pomme a travaillé sur un Pencil plus court spécialement conçu pour le Duo, mais le projet aurait été totalement abandonné. Cependant, surprise, Apple a annoncé lors de sa dernière keynote que le Duo était compatible avec le Pencil USB-C, soit le stylet vendu pour les iPad. Mais quand celui-ci pourra-t-il être supporté par le logiciel de l’iPhone Duo ? Il va falloir attendre des précisions de la part d’Apple.

articles.title: Galaxy Buds 4 com ANC volta a receber 38% de desconto no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Buds 4 com ANC volta a receber 38% de desconto no Mercado Livre
Galaxy Buds 4 traz agentes de IA integrados, cancelamento ativo de ruido e função para chamadas; pague no Pix e use o cupom HOJETEMPROMO válido somente até o final do dia
O Galaxy Buds 4 voltou a receber nesta segunda-feira (28) um desconto de 38% no Mercado Livre. Os fones de ouvido de última geração saem por R$ 989,01 no Pix com o cupom HOJETEMPROMO. No entanto, o cupom tem validade até o final do dia ou até que esgote, aproveite esse preço o quanto antes.
O wearable utiliza o Samsung Seamless Codec com áudio Hi-Fi de 24 bits, proporcionando uma experiência sonora amplamente fiel as frequências originais das músicas. A qualidade para ligações não fica atrás, já que possui a função Chamadas Ultra Nítidas, apoiada por seis microfones integrados e alto-falantes de 11 mm que resultam em um áudio limpo.
O Galaxy Buds 4 conta com cancelamento ativo de ruído (ANC) adaptativo, ou seja, consegue alterar o nível de vedação a depender do nível de decibéis do ambiente. Segundo a Samsung, a função foi otimizada para a nova geração dos fones e mostra ser bem útil para usar em academia ou no transporte público, por exemplo.
A inteligência artificial está presente por meio de agentes como Perplexity, Gemini, Bixby e o Galaxy AI. Os assistentes entre uma série de funções disponíveis, podem auxiliar o usuário com lembretes referentes a compromissos na agenda, notificações recebidas e dúvidas no geral.
Equipado com Bluetooth 6.1, o fone da Samsung garantem uma conexão estável e com baixa latência. Além disso, o suporte ao Auto Switch facilita a troca de pareamento entre dispositivos Galaxy. Em relação a autonomia, a bateria entrega até 30 horas de reprodução com o estojo de recarga, mas apenas 5 horas com o ANC ativado.
Os sensores de proximidade e toque facilitam o uso no dia a dia ao possibilitar gerenciar o volume, pular, voltar ou até pausar a música automaticamente ao retirá-los. Além disso, o Áudio 360 e o equalizador adaptativo ajustam as frequências para proporcionar uma experiência sonora tridimensional e personalizada.
O Galaxy Buds 4 com resistência moderada a poeira e proteção contra respingos d’água está disponível por R$ 989,01 no Pix com o cupom HOJETEMPROMO no Mercado Livre.

articles.title: Anvisa notifica Mercado Livre por venda de medicamentos em marketplace
articles.text:
A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) notificou o Mercado Livre após a empresa anunciar a criação de uma drogaria própria para operar dentro de seu marketplace e comercializar medicamentos e outros produtos sujeitos à vigilância sanitária pela internet. A informação foi antecipada pela Folha de S.Paulo e confirmada pelo g1 nesta terça-feira (29).
Segundo a agência, a notificação solicita informações sobre a regularidade da empresa para exercer esse tipo de atividade, incluindo o cumprimento das exigências sanitárias aplicáveis a farmácias e drogarias. A Anvisa afirmou ainda que, até o momento, não existe previsão normativa que autorize marketplaces a intermediar a comercialização de medicamentos.
Entre os documentos solicitados estão a identificação e o endereço da empresa responsável pela drogaria, a autorização de funcionamento emitida pela Anvisa, o alvará sanitário e a identificação do farmacêutico responsável técnico.
A agência também pediu informações sobre os procedimentos utilizados para conferir receitas médicas e sobre as regras adotadas para armazenamento e transporte dos medicamentos.
O Mercado Livre terá três dias úteis, a partir do recebimento da notificação, para apresentar os documentos e esclarecimentos solicitados. O prazo termina nesta quinta-feira (1).
Anvisa ainda regulamenta atuação de plataformas
- A posição da Anvisa ocorre em meio a mudança recente nas regras para a comercialização de medicamentos por canais digitais;
- Em agosto, a agência informou que a revogação de medidas que proibiam a comercialização e a propaganda de medicamentos em plataformas digitais — incluindo o próprio Mercado Livre — não representava uma autorização automática para a venda de produtos farmacêuticos;
- Segundo a Anvisa, a aplicação da nova legislação dependia de regulamentação específica ainda a ser editada pela agência;
- Dias depois, em 19 de agosto, a Diretoria Colegiada da Anvisa aprovou a abertura de processo administrativo justamente para regulamentar a contratação, por farmácias, de canais digitais e plataformas de comércio eletrônico para logística e entrega ao consumidor. A iniciativa busca adequar as regras sanitárias à Lei 15.357/2026;
- É nesse contexto que a agência questiona o modelo anunciado pelo Mercado Livre.
Abrafarma questionou operação
O anúncio também levou a Associação Brasileira de Redes de Farmácias e Drogarias (Abrafarma) a procurar a Anvisa. Em ofício enviado à agência em 25 de setembro, a entidade pediu esclarecimentos urgentes sobre a regularidade sanitária do modelo anunciado pelo Mercado Livre.
A Anvisa afirmou que a medida faz parte de sua atividade de fiscalização, sem atribuir a ação ao documento da Abrafarma.
No ofício, a entidade afirma ter tomado conhecimento de que o Mercado Livre pretendia integrar redes de farmácias ao marketplace em um modelo chamado de 3P, no qual estabelecimentos de terceiros oferecem seus produtos dentro da plataforma.
A associação argumenta que o anúncio levantava dúvidas porque a própria Anvisa já havia informado anteriormente que mudanças recentes na legislação não significavam uma autorização automática para a comercialização de produtos farmacêuticos por plataformas digitais.
Segundo o documento, em agosto, a agência havia informado que a aplicação da nova regra dependia de regulamentação específica e que os efeitos concretos da autorização legal para o uso de canais digitais e plataformas de comércio eletrônico só ocorreriam após a complementação das normas pela Anvisa.
A entidade também lembra que existe um processo regulatório em andamento para definir os requisitos sanitários para esse tipo de operação, incluindo questões, como rastreabilidade, responsabilidade técnica e limites de atuação das plataformas digitais.
Leia mais:
- Golpe usa falso app do Mercado Livre para invadir celulares
- Mercado Livre e Mercado Pago são alvo de pedido do Idec para investigar reconhecimento facial
- Anvisa aprova nova caneta para diabetes que combina insulina e semaglutida em aplicação semanal
O que a Abrafarma pediu à Anvisa
Entre os questionamentos enviados à agência, a Abrafarma perguntou se, antes da conclusão da regulamentação, já é permitida a comercialização de medicamentos por farmácias e drogarias de terceiros integradas a um marketplace.
A associação também pediu esclarecimentos sobre a possibilidade de uma plataforma participar de etapas, como exposição dos produtos, busca, seleção, intermediação da compra ou realização da transação envolvendo medicamentos antes da edição das novas regras.
Outro questionamento foi sobre quais providências seriam adotadas caso esse modelo não esteja autorizado atualmente e se a participação de farmácias regularmente licenciadas seria suficiente para alterar o entendimento de que a operação depende de regulamentação específica.
No documento, a Abrafarma afirma que não se opõe ao uso de tecnologia ou a novos modelos de logística e entrega no varejo farmacêutico. A entidade, porém, defende que as mudanças sejam implementadas dentro das regras sanitárias, com segurança jurídica e isonomia entre as empresas do setor.
Mercado Livre diz não ter sido notificado
Em nota, o Mercado Livre afirma que, até o momento, não havia recebido qualquer notificação ou informação referente ao ofício mencionado. A empresa também declarou que cumpre as normas aplicáveis e coloca a segurança dos usuários em primeiro lugar.
Segundo o Mercado Livre, a entrada na venda de medicamentos seguirá essa mesma orientação. A empresa afirma ainda que seus produtos possuem rastreabilidade completa, com controle de origem e validade, e que mantém diálogo com a Anvisa e outras entidades para contribuir com a adaptação da regulamentação.
A empresa já havia anunciado a entrada na venda de medicamentos com prescrição médica, incluindo antibióticos e remédios para emagrecimento, por meio de sua própria farmácia. O plano também prevê a participação de redes farmacêuticas na plataforma.
A discussão, portanto, ocorre enquanto a Anvisa ainda trabalha na regulamentação específica para a atuação de canais digitais e plataformas de comércio eletrônico na logística e entrega de medicamentos.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Apple quiere lanzar productos todo el año y su nuevo CEO ya tiene un plan para lograrlo
articles.text:
Una de las cosas que caracteriza a Apple es que siempre llega tarde a la fiesta cuando de nuevos productos o tecnologías se trata. Los de Cupertino nunca son los primeros, pero esos años de retraso se traducen en una mejor experiencia cuando se comparan con otras tecnológicas. Esta idea podría desaparecer, ya que el nuevo CEO quiere acelerar el desarrollo y adaptarse a la velocidad que exige la inteligencia artificial.
De acuerdo con Bloomberg, John Ternus quiere que Apple presente productos con más frecuencia a lo largo del año. El nuevo director ejecutivo no está de acuerdo en que la compañía solo dependa de sus dos eventos especiales (primavera y otoño) para anunciar sus novedades. Ternus desea que la compañía se vuelva más experimental para seguir siendo competitiva.
La idea de lanzar dispositivos fuera de septiembre o marzo no suena descabellada, aunque no es muy sencilla de implementar. Algunos empleados advierten que modificar unas prácticas de desarrollo tan arraigadas podría tomar años. No obstante, toda la plantilla deberá ajustarse y modificar sus hojas de ruta para cumplir con el mandato, sobre todo si no quiere sufrir caídas de ingresos como las que experimentaron algunas de sus divisiones en trimestres anteriores.
La prueba de fuego para que Apple ponga en práctica esta mentalidad podría ocurrir tan pronto como el próximo año. La tecnológica planea lanzar sus primeras gafas inteligentes, unos AirPods con cámara y un iPhone rediseñado para conmemorar el vigésimo aniversario del dispositivo. Ternus planearía lanzamientos escalonados durante el año, lo cual empujaría los ingresos en sus divisiones de hardware y servicios.
Apple despide a empleados para volverse más ágil
Es probable que este plan sea complicado de implementar durante sus primeras fases, pero el nuevo CEO planea transformar la compañía para mantenerla en el Top 3 de empresas tecnológicas. No es un secreto que Apple perdió el rumbo con la inteligencia artificial y priorizó otros desarrollos cuando tenía que invertir más en sus modelos. El descalabro de Siri con Apple Intelligence fue tan grande que tuvieron que reiniciar todo y depender de Google para poder ofrecer una IA competitiva en el iPhone.
John Ternus también quiere que la empresa se vuelva más ágil y esto implica reducir la burocracia al desarrollar productos. Desde que dirigía la división de hardware, el directivo anticipó que Apple debe lograr más con menos personas y ahora está aplicando un recorte en varios de sus departamentos internos. Según el periodista Mark Gurman, Apple ha despedido a varios gerentes de producto y directivos en las últimas dos semanas.
Los despidos han sido una constante en Apple desde que comenzó la reestructuración a inicios de 2025. Este reajuste fue más notorio en divisiones como Siri o Vision Pro, que sufrieron bajas considerables junto a los equipos de IA y Fitness+. A lo anterior se suma el retiro de algunos ejecutivos que llevaban décadas en la compañía, incluido Tim Cook.
El nuevo CEO de Apple tiene una tarea difícil, ya que no solo tiene que rediseñar los procesos de desarrollo, sino también lidiar con una de las crisis de hardware más complejas de los últimos años. La demanda de los centros de datos ha generado una escasez de memoria que encareció los componentes de prácticamente todos los dispositivos, incluido el iPhone.

articles.title: Dutch police arrest ShinyHunters hacker accused of planning two murders | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The FBI and Dutch law enforcement say they have arrested a member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which the agencies say are responsible for hacks on over 140 organizations around the world. The hackers also claimed responsibility for a breach of the FBI’s own systems earlier this month.
Brett Leathermann, the FBI’s cyber division lead, said in a video message on Tuesday that Dutch authorities had arrested one of the “alleged leaders of ShinyHunters.” Leathermann added that the Dutch High Tech Crime Unit “moved quickly to protect victims and preserve critical evidence,” and vowed that the bureau would go after the rest of the hackers following the arrest.
In a separate statement, Dutch police confirmed that an unnamed 24-year-old man from Amsterdam was arrested under Dutch law on September 15. The man was scheduled to appear in court on Tuesday, and has been remanded into custody for at least 90 days.
The police say the man was arrested for “participating in a criminal organization,” referring to ShinyHunters.
Following his arrest and seizure of his devices, the police said “a lot of information was found on his laptop, including about two murders that should be committed abroad.” As such, he is also being investigated for attempting to orchestrate the murders. The Dutch authorities said this is “separate from the investigation into ShinyHunters.”
ShinyHunters is a cyber criminal gang that are accused of hacking into companies to steal reams of data and then threatening to publish the data if its victims do not pay a ransom. The Dutch authorities said the gang are accused of data breaches at Pornhub, Ticketmaster, and U.S. telco giant AT&T. The hacking group also took responsibility for a breach of Dutch phone provider Odido. However, the authorities said that the man they took into custody has not been arrested in relation to the Odido hack.
Independent security journalist Brian Krebs, who was first to report the arrest, and other media outlets have named the arrested man as Pepijn van der Stap, who was profiled by Bloomberg in 2024 as a cybersecurity researcher who also moonlighted as a criminal hacker who extorted companies.
According to recent reporting by Bloomberg and Reuters, Van der Stap was arrested earlier this month by police at the offices of Neo Security, where Van der Stap is employed as chief technology officer. The raid reportedly involved flash-bang grenades.
A representative for Neo Security did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment. When asked by TechCrunch, a representative of the ShinyHunters group told TechCrunch that Van der Stap “has no association with us.”
News of the arrest comes days after the FBI reportedly told its own agents and employees that their personal information, including their names, addresses, job titles and Social Security numbers, were exposed in a “cyber security incident.” The FBI has not yet publicly confirmed a breach, but the ShinyHunters gang said it took personal and sensitive data belonging to “mostly all” of the FBI’s agents and applicants by breaching its careers website and job application portal.
Among the sample of 5,000 or so agents who had data stolen from the portal, reporters have also found data relating to agents’ blood and urine samples, as well as psychiatric reports, which sparked fears of a major counterintelligence challenge to prevent an adversarial government from obtaining the data.
When contacted by TechCrunch, Leathermann did not comment. An FBI spokesperson declined to comment on our questions relating to the arrest.
For their part, the ShinyHunters hackers reiterated that the breach of the FBI’s servers was not a financially motivated attack, but was intended to challenge public claims made by the FBI, which the hackers say contain false allegations about the group. The hackers told TechCrunch that they will not publish the stolen FBI data, and added that the breach was “to make a point and to dispute the allegations made against us and we have done so.”

articles.title: Suspected ShinyHunters leader arrested in the Netherlands
articles.text:
Dutch police say they arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam man in connection with ShinyHunters, the hacking group that claimed responsibility for high-profile attacks on Ticketmaster, Rockstar Games, and more recently, the FBI. In a press release, Dutch authorities state that they arrested the suspect on September 15th — just days before the hacking group claimed to have breached the FBI’s website and stolen employee data, as reported earlier by Reuters.
Suspected ShinyHunters leader arrested in the Netherlands
The 24-year-old man is linked to the hacking group behind attacks on the FBI, Rockstar Games, Ticketmaster, and more.
Neither Dutch authorities nor the FBI name the suspect, but Krebs on Security and Reuters report that police arrested Pepijn van der Stap, a Dutch man convicted for data theft and extortion in 2023. Van der Stap joined the Dutch cybersecurity company Neo Security when he was released from prison last year, according to Krebs on Security. ShinyHunters tells Reuters that Van der Stap has “no association” with the group.
Brett Leatherman, the FBI’s Cyber Division Assistant Director, calls the suspect one of the group’s alleged leaders, while issuing a warning to remaining members. “The longer you stay in this, the more we learn about you. You know how to find us, and we know how to find you,” Leatherman says in a video published on Tuesday. “I suggest you reach out first while the choice is still yours.”
The 24-year-old is also suspected of “attempted incitement to commit two murders,” according to the Dutch police. “As we speak FBI teams are actively working with partners to obtain and execute more leads in the ongoing investigation based on this arrest,” FBI Director Kash Patel writes in a post on X.

articles.title: Avec le SurroundPlay, JBL transforme les enceintes Bluetooth en satellites Surround
articles.text:
Le bonheur, c’est la liberté. JBL expérimente déjà ce concept avec ses barres de son haut de gamme, comme la Bar 1300MK2 et ses enceintes Surround détachables. Avec sa nouvelle gamme Cinema SB MK2, la marque pousse le concept bien plus loin, et permet enfin d’utiliser les enceintes Bluetooth portables de son catalogue pour les canaux Surround. Une avancée intéressante pour l’écosystème JBL, qui devrait rendre sa gamme home-cinéma nettement plus attractive.
Quatre barres de son d’entrée et de milieu de gamme ont été annoncées pour le moment : SB595MK2, SB580MK2, SB550MK2, et la petite SB510MK2. La marque s’appuie sur des ensembles simples, à savoir des barres de taille moyenne, sans enceinte Surround intégrés dans le packaging, pour des architectures allant du 3.1.2 au 3.1. L’idée est de proposer une expérience abordable mais modulaire, grâce à la technologie SurroundPlay.
SurroundPlay : l’arme secrète pour l’immersion
N’allant pour le moment pas trop dans les détails, JBL présente l’arme secrète de cette nouvelle gamme : le SurroundPlay. Cette technologie permet, via une simple pression sur la barre, de l’associer à une paire d’enceintes Bluetooth JBL afin d’envoyer le flux des canaux Surround sur cette dernière. Il ne semble malheureusement pas possible d’utiliser une unique enceinte, qui assurerait le rôle d’enceinte Surround d’ambiance par exemple (en position centrale derrière la position d’écoute).
Le principe, qui s’appuie probablement sur les capacités LE Audio des récentes barres de son et des enceintes Bluetooth JBL, demeure toutefois propriétaire. Le SurroundPlay complète ainsi les capacités Surround des enceintes JBL Cove présentées ce mois-ci, les deux technologies (différentes) exploitant enfin le très large catalogue de la marque. Tempérons tout de même notre enthousiasme, puisque seule la Flip 7 sera compatible à la sortie des Cinema SB MK2. Nous pouvons évidemment espérer une mise à jour des autres enceintes Bluetooth LE Audio/Auracast.
Un quatuor simple et abordable
Quatre produits constituent la première fournée. Le modèle le plus haut de gamme, bien qu’assez abordable, est le SB595MK2. Il se compose d’une barre de son avec voie centrale dédiée et haut-parleurs verticaux (Atmos), ainsi que d’un caisson de basses avec woofer de 6,5 pouces. Cette barre intègre une entrée HDMI, un port HDMI eARC, et revendique une puissance de 440 W. Son prix est annoncé à 449,99 euros. Petite particularité, qu'elle partage avec le SB580MK2 et le SB550MK2, la barre peut se plier en U, particularité qui permet surtout de gagner de la place pour le transport.
Version légèrement simplifiée, la SB580MK2 reprend à l’identique le format et les capacités de sa grande sœur, mais fait l’impasse sur les haut-parleurs Atmos. Son prix est évidemment allégé : 349,99 euros.
Encore un peu plus simple car moins puissante, sans entrée HDMI, et ne prenant pas en charge les flux Dolby Atmos, la SB550MK2 est une barre 3.1 livrée avec un petit caisson de basses (woofer de 5,25 pouces). Elle conserve heureusement la compatibilité Auracast. Son tarif passe à 249,99 euros.
Enfin, la SB510MK2 est une simple unité 3.1/3.0 livrée sans caisson, et non pliable. Il est évident que l’association avec des enceintes Bluetooth en configuration Surround améliorera grandement l’ordinaire. La SB510MK2 est annoncée à seulement 199,99 euros.
Tout juste annoncée, la gamme JBL Cinema SB MK2 sera disponible dès le1 er octobre 2026.

articles.title: Précommande Lego Dragon Ball : prix, date de sortie et où acheter le set Shenron et Goku
articles.text:
Depuis ses débuts en 1984 dans les pages du Weekly Shōnen Jump, Dragon Ball est devenu l’un des mangas les plus influents de la pop culture, marquant plusieurs générations de lecteurs et de spectateurs à travers le monde. Les fans devront attendre le 4 novembre 2026 pour mettre la main sur le premier set Lego officiel consacré à l’univers d’Akira Toriyama. Le Lego Icons Dragon Ball : Shenron & Goku réunit ainsi le dragon sacré et le jeune Goku dans une imposante construction de 1 764 pièces.
Quand et où acheter le Lego Dragon Ball : Shenron & Goku ?
Le Groupe Lego et Toei Animation s’associent pour ce premier set issu de la licence Dragon Ball, qui met en scène Shenron lors de son invocation, avec Goku installé sur son Kinto-un tandis que le dragon s’élève au-dessus des sept Dragon Balls. Affiché à 139,99 € sur le Lego Store, il sera disponible dès le 1er novembre 2026 pour les membres Lego Insiders, avant une sortie généralisé et chez les autres détaillants le 4 novembre. D’autres sets Dragon Ball sont également annoncés pour 2027.
C’est quoi, ce Lego Dragon Ball ?
Le Lego Icons Dragon Ball : Shenron & Goku s’adresse aux fans, qu’ils aient découvert Dragon Ball avec le manga d’Akira Toriyama ou avec son adaptation en anime. Avec ses écailles ondulées et ses griffes sculptées, cette réplique de Shenron, le dragon sacré, est présentée dans une posture dynamique, enroulée sur elle-même et s’élevant au-dessus des sept Dragon Balls, comme s’il venait tout juste d’être invoqué. Il s’accompagne d’une minifigurine de Goku enfant sur son Kinto-un, qu’il est possible de repositionner autour du fameux dragon.
Lego explique que ses designers ont étudié des images de la première série animée pour retranscrire la silhouette de Shenron. Plusieurs techniques de construction ont ainsi été utilisées pour donner vie à ses écailles, sa forme sinueuse et ses nombreux détails sculptés. C’est une réussite : sur les visuels officiels, Shenron reste immédiatement reconnaissable dans sa version briques.
Avec ses 1 764 pièces, le modèle est avant tout pensé comme une véritable pièce d’exposition. La tête et les griffes de Shenron sont orientables. La figurine mesure plus de 32 cm de haut, 24 cm de long et 26 cm de large. Lego n’a pas encore dévoilé quels personnages ni quelles périodes de la saga couvriront les sets prévus en 2027.

articles.title: Nigerian startup Adaptive Atelier building accessibility infrastructure for digital products - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Adaptive Atelier is building the technology infrastructure businesses need to make their digital products accessible, and to prove that accessibility actually works for the disabled people it is meant to serve.
Founded in 2024 by Toyosi Badejo-Okusanya, and headquartered across Lagos and London, Adaptive Atelier operates three connected products.
AdaptiveTest is an AI-powered scanner that analyses websites and digital products against WCAG accessibility standards; AdaptiveWiz is an accessibility API, with live Shopify and WordPress integrations that helps disabled users personalise and navigate digital experiences; and AdaptiveAlly is a marketplace connecting businesses with vetted disabled professionals who test whether accessibility fixes work in practice.
“AdaptiveTest identifies the problem, AdaptiveWiz helps fix the experience, and AdaptiveAlly validates whether the fix actually holds up for a real disabled user. That closes a loop that automated tools alone cannot close,” Badejo-Okusanya told Disrupt Africa.
She said most businesses already know accessibility matters, and are under growing pressure from customers, regulators and digital transformation to act on it.
“The gap we identified is the distance between knowing accessibility matters and actually having the infrastructure to identify, fix, and validate it,” she said.
The existing market, Badejo-Okusanya said, is fragmented across automated scanners and overlay widgets, which are quick to deploy but limited in what they can detect and fix; traditional consultancies, which offer deep expertise but little proprietary technology; and generic user-testing platforms not built around disabled testers.
“We sit at the intersection of these categories, combining AI-driven detection and remediation with structured, paid validation from disabled professionals, rather than asking a business to choose between automation and lived-experience insight,” she said.
The startup has built a community of over 13,000 disabled professionals and advocates, giving the AdaptiveAlly marketplace a ready supply side, while its website draws around 50,000 organic visits a month. It has carried out customer discovery with disabled professionals across the United Kingdom (UK), Nigeria, Canada, Germany, Morocco and the United States (US), as well as with enterprise compliance and digital leaders.
Adaptive Atelier has begun signing paying customers across cinemas, government institutions and retail platforms, and counts L’Oréal, SignHealth, Channel 4 and Phonak among the organisations it has active relationships with.
The company makes money through subscriptions for AdaptiveWiz, scoped audits for AdaptiveTest, and commission on AdaptiveAlly marketplace transactions.
“A business often enters through an AdaptiveTest audit, which surfaces the case for AdaptiveWiz as an ongoing fix, and AdaptiveAlly as the validation layer that proves it’s working,” Badejo-Okusanya said. “The priority right now is proving a repeatable path from first engagement to long-term customer before pushing for more volume.”
The startup has been self-funded to date, and is now raising a US$250,000 institutional round to support technical hiring and go-to-market execution. Badejo-Okusanya was a finalist in the Standard Chartered Foundation Women in Tech Accelerator Nigeria, and Adaptive Atelier is currently part of the Synergies Work Igniting Ideas Business Accelerator in the US, sponsored by the Mitsubishi Electric Foundation.
Nigeria remains the startup’s home market, but it is building early relationships in the UK, European Union (EU) and US, where regulation such as the European Accessibility Act and ADA requirements is creating urgency for enterprise buyers.
The road has not been without challenges. Badejo-Okusanya said product delivery slipped against expectations at one stage, forcing the company to rebuild parts of its technical roadmap and team.
“We now treat rigorous internal testing before external claims as non-negotiable,” she said.
Market education has been another hurdle, with many businesses still viewing accessibility as a compliance cost rather than a commercial opportunity, while focus has also been key.
“With genuine interest from both African and Western markets, the discipline has been choosing where to concentrate go-to-market effort first, rather than spreading a small team across two very different buyer types at once,” Badejo-Okusanya said.

articles.title: TechSparks 2026: More founders, tech leaders, global policymakers shaping the New Tech Order
articles.text:
TechSparks 2026: More founders, tech leaders, global policymakers shaping the New Tech Order
From AI and deeptech to fintech, aerospace, and digital infrastructure, TechSparks 2026 convenes the builders and policymakers redefining how technology is created, scaled, and governed.
Technology isn’t just being shaped by founders and engineers anymore; policymakers, global institutions, and industry leaders are also a vital part of the conversation.
At TechSparks 2026, YourStory's flagship startup and technology summit, that conversation will span policy, deeptech, AI, fintech, aerospace, mobility, and digital infrastructure. The speakers taking the stage include Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, IT, BT & E-Governance, Government of Karnataka, and Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, Government of Karnataka.
With the theme ‘The New Tech Order’, TechSparks 2026 will look at how AI, deeptech, and new digital infrastructure are changing how technology gets built and scaled. The three-day event will take place from October 13-15 in Bengaluru.
Here are some of the other speakers joining the TechSparks 2026 lineup:
Dr Angela Honegger
Dr Angela Honegger is CEO and Consul General, Switzerland and India, Federal Department of Foreign Affairs. Based in Bengaluru, she is also associated with Swissnex in India, the Swiss science and technology network that connects Switzerland with the country's innovation ecosystem. Her background includes work across Switzerland, India, and the US, along with experience in entrepreneurship, innovation, and research.
Revant Himatsingka
Revant Himatsingka, better known as the Food Pharmer, is the founder of Only What's Needed, a food and beverage venture built around transparency. Himatsingka has built a large public following around reading food labels and questioning how packaged food is marketed.
With Only What’s Needed, that focus has moved from educating consumers to building a food brand around transparency. The company says it is building food together with consumers, while Himatsingka has also shared product decisions and business information publicly as the company has grown.
Peter Winther-Schmidt
Peter Winther-Schmidt, Consul General at the Consulate General of Denmark in Bangalore, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark, represents the India-Denmark relationship in the TechSparks lineup. articles.title: Former US Air Force members sent to prison over BEC attacks
articles.text:
Two former members of the United States Air Force were sentenced to a combined 189 months in federal prison for their roles in a multi-year series of business email compromise (BEC) scams and phishing campaigns.
According to court documents, 25-year-old Chijioke Timothy Odimegwu and 26-year-old Harafat Mogaji carried out these attacks while stationed at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware.
They stole victims' employee email credentials in spamming and phishing campaigns. The defendants then used "spoofed" email addresses that mimicked business partners' emails, along with the credentials, to redirect payments to accounts controlled by accomplices in the United States and abroad.
Odimegwu and Mogaji also made financial transactions without the victims' knowledge using their stolen financial information (e.g., account information, personal identification numbers, and credit and debit card numbers) and additional data bought from their partners in crime.
"Working with co-conspirators both in the United States and abroad, Odimegwu and Mogaji fraudulently diverted a more than $1.68 million wire sent by a victim in Iowa City, Iowa, to a bank account in Chicago controlled by the conspiracy," the Department of Justice said in a Tuesday press release.
"They also diverted a more than $720,000 wire sent by a victim in Ohio to a bank account controlled by the conspiracy. These are in addition to many other attempts Odimegwu and Mogaji made to divert wire transfers made by businesses in Iowa and across the country."
Odimegwu was sentenced to 111 months in prison and ordered to pay $366,617.59 in restitution, while Mogaji got 78 months and was ordered to pay $995,680.45 in restitution. After completing their federal prison terms, they will both have to serve a three-year term on supervised release.
In BEC scams, cybercriminals redirect legitimate corporate payments to attacker-controlled bank accounts by using victims' compromised email addresses to trick billing departments into approving new banking information.
When they receive the payment, the attackers quickly drain the account using money mules or transfer the funds to various other accounts they control to evade court orders that mandate the funds be frozen.
BEC attacks can severely impact victims' operations because of the massive financial losses they can inflict. As the FBI revealed in its 2025 Internet Crime Report, business email compromise remains a major cyber threat, with 24,768 complaints and over $3 billion in losses logged last year.
Earlier this year, in July, Ghanaian national Derrick Van Yeboah (who was extradited to the U.S. in August 2025) was sentenced to 85 months in prison after being extradited to the U.S. in August 2025 and pleading guilty in March 2026 to his role as a high-ranking member of a massive fraud ring that stole over $100 million from victims across the United States in business email compromise attacks and romance scams.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: Nothing dévoile le Headphone (1) Pro : trois transducteurs, 46 dB de réduction de bruit et du son Hi-Res
articles.text:
Après le Headphone (1) sorti en juillet 2025, Nothing est de retour avec le Headphone (1) Pro. Le constructeur britannique présente son nouveau casque audio comme « fait pour le studio ». Il faut dire que les réglages sonores ont été confiés à un studio d’enregistrement londonien. Par ailleurs, le casque audio intègre pas moins de trois transducteurs. Spécificités, réduction de bruit, prix… : voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir.
Trois transducteurs et des réglages sonores confiés à un studio d’enregistrement
Le Headphone (1), sorti en juillet 2025, présentait un transducteur de 40 mm. Le Headphone (1) Pro en intègre quant à lui trois de chaque côté. Il s’agit sans aucun doute de l’amélioration la plus notable. Pour être plus précis, un transducteur dynamique de 40 mm est chargé de restituer les basses, tandis qu’un autre gère les médiums. Un troisième transducteur, un driver xMEMS gravé dans du silicium, s’occupe quant à lui des aigus. Chaque plage sonore est ainsi traitée séparément, ce qui offre une restitution sonore bien plus précise. À noter que chaque transducteur peut être réglé individuellement dans les réglages.
Nothing explique que son nouveau casque est « fait pour le studio ». Pour appuyer son propos, le constructeur explique avoir confié les réglages sonores au studio d’enregistrement londonien Metropolis Studios. Ce dernier a réglé cinq profils d’égalisation qui « mettent en valeur des genres britanniques comme le Neo-Jazz, le Rock, le UK Rap + Grime, l’Electronica et la Bass ». Le studio londonien a également mis au point le mode Flat EQ qui propose un son sans coloration ni traitement artificiel. Un bouton physique sur le casque permet par ailleurs d’activer ou de désactiver ce mode à tout moment.
Notons enfin qu’en filaire, le port USB-C permet de profiter d’un son sans perte jusqu’en 24 bits/192 kHz, soit une définition supérieure à celle d’un CD, limitée à 16 bits/44,1 kHz. En Bluetooth, le Headphone (1) Pro prend également en charge le format LDAC.
Réduction de bruit, connectivité et prix
Nothing annonce jusqu’à 46 dB de réduction de bruit active grâce à dix micros intégrés au casque et à une nouvelle isolation acoustique en silicone. Pour rappel, le Headphone (1) de 2025 offrait une réduction de bruit jusqu’à 42 dB. Côté connectivité, le Headphone (1) Pro prend en charge le Bluetooth 6.1, l’Auracast et la connexion simultanée à deux appareils. Enfin, notons que Nothing annonce jusqu’à 68 h d’autonomie sans la réduction de bruit activée. Il faudra voir ce qu’il en est avec l’ANC activée. Le Headphone (1) Pro est disponible dès aujourd’hui en noir ou en blanc au prix de vente conseillé de 349 euros.
